Heading: Chiranjeevi reaches out to BJP, poll alliance likely - Indian Express
Content:
Defence Minister AK Antony will undertake his maiden visit to the US next month to enhance defence partnerships. Antony, who will visit the country from September 7-10, will be accompanied by top defence officials and senior officers including Defence Secretary Vijay Singh.

The agenda for Antony's visit has not been revealed but the minister is expected to meet top US officials including Defence Secretary Robert Gates - and hold discussions on the growing defence trade between the two countries besides looking for new areas of collaboration in the area of defence research.

With defence trade between the countries taking off, a number of key protocols are expected to be signed shortly.

Heading: Manmohan for PM again: Cong not so sure now - Indian Express
Content:
Telugu superstar Chiranjeevi called up BJP leader L K Advani on Monday to inform him about his party's launch on August 26. "The actor has been in touch with the BJP. Advaniji wished him well for the launch," said BJP sources.

The BJP leader is also believed to have told the actor, whose party is giving both the Opposition Telugu Desam Party and ruling Congress in the state the jitters, that the country needs "more good people like him in politics". The superstar met senior BJP leader M Venkaiah Naidu in Chennai last month.

Hailing from the preponderant Kapu community, the actor, nursing chief ministerial ambitions, got in touch with the BJP top brass some six months back. His brother-in-law Allu Arvind is said to be a key interlocutor in talks with various parties. The superstar has also been in touch with the Left and even the BSP for "some kind of arrangement for the Assembly elections". "He is in touch with various parties; but has not taken a call on a tie-up for the Assembly polls," said a leader.

BJP sources said that while the saffron party has hardly any presence in the state, Chiranjeevi might want to have "an anchor in a national party." "Any kind of tie-up with the BJP will give the actor, who will otherwise win sizeable seats in coastal districts, a boost in the Telangana region," claimed a BJP leader.

Parties like the TDP have, however, kept away from the BJP for the fear of losing out on the Muslim votes in the state. The BJP is nevertheless hopeful that the actor will extend his post-poll support to the NDA due to "his anti-Congress stance."

Advani has also been banking on "soft power" in the run-up to the polls. The strategy involves hard-selling his book (Spin doctors are trying to make at least 10,000 people read its Hindi translation in Uttar Pradesh), apart from getting personalities ranging from Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, Mammootty to Aamir Khan to share the public platform with Advani. Chiranjeevi may well be the latest to join the bandwagon, feels the party.

Heading: Left divided over going with Maya - Indian Express
Content:
Three days after Congress president Sonia Gandhi virtually declared Manmohan Singh the party's prime ministerial candidate for the next Lok Sabha election, the ruling party appeared to be doing a rethink on it as it sought to skirt the issue on Monday.

"The issue is not on the table yet. Election is seven-eight months away," AICC spokesperson Manish Tewari said in response to a query whether Manmohan Singh was now the UPA's prime ministerial candidate.

On August 15, responding to queries from reporters at the Congress headquarters whether he would unfurl the tricolour from the ramparts of the Red Fort again next year , when Prime Minister Manmohan Singh had said "hopefully", the Congress president had hastened to assert, "Certainly, I am saying certainly".

Heading: Panel’s CPM member for lie-detector test on Saxena - Indian Express
Content:
The Left may have decided to launch a joint campaign with the BSP and the UNPA against the UPA Government, but there is a growing sense of uneasiness in the bloc with the smaller parties feeling wary of the newfound friendship with Mayawati.

Though talks of the Left entering into any sort of electoral understanding with the BSP and parties of the United National Progressive Alliance for the next Lok Sabha polls may be in the realm of speculation, parties like the RSP and Forward Bloc seem not too enthusiastic about such an arrangement.

Initially upset with big brother CPI(M) for not taking it into confidence before Prakash Karat's July 13 meeting with Mayawati, the RSP is also unhappy with CPI general secretary A B Bardhan's open talks about Mayawati being a fit candidate for the post of Prime Minister.

"It is too early for such talks. The present arrangement is limited to a joint campaign on issues like inflation and the Indo-US nuclear deal; such talks will only complicate matters," a senior Left leader said.

While the CPI(M) and the CPI are apparently in favour of exploring the options of joining hands with secular parties who are not aligned either with the BJP or the Congress, RSP and the Forward Bloc feel stress should be laid on greater Left unity first given the fickle nature of regional parties.

"The Left front concept is at present limited to Kerala, Tripura and West Bengal. The arrangement should first be extended to other states where we have some presence," a senior Left leader said while questioning the wisdom of joining hands with Mayawati.

A section of the CPI(M) and leaders of the RSP and Forward Bloc also argue that alliances with regional parties for electoral gains will have long-term implications as it would not help the Left in its efforts to make inroads into states where they are weak, particularly the Hindi heartland.

"The idea of a third force or third alternative to counter the BJP and the Congress may be a good election idea. But unless and until there is a united Left force, efforts to strengthen our respective party organisations in other states will not go a long way," RSP leader Abani Roy told The Indian Express.

Moreover, some leaders feel the alliance with parties like the BSP may become a baggage, as the Left will have to sacrifice its position on certain issues. One Left leader pointed out that neither the CPI(M) nor the CPI openly condemned the recent police firing on agitating farmers in Greater Noida. The Left even had to speak out against the CBI lodging cases against Mayawati in a disproportionate assets case.

"The question is about credibility. We should not be seen as desperate for allies and compromising our policy positions. We should be condemning police excesses," a senior Left leader said.

Though neither the CPI(M) nor the CPI has commented on AIADMK supremo J Jayalalithaa's recent statement that she was open to a tie-up with the Left, the smaller Left parties are skeptical on this count as well.

Heading: Nationwide stir: Left makes no exception for IT, SEZs - Indian Express
Content:
As sanjeev Saxena, an alleged aide of Samajwadi Party general secretary Amar Singh, denied any involvement in the cash-for-vote scam, CPI(M) member Mohammad Salim, a member of the special Lok Sabha committee headed by V Kishore Chandra Deo, on Monday demanded that he be put through a lie-detector test.

According to sources in the committee, which met for three hours, Salim's demand was promptly endorsed by Vijay Kumar Malhotra of the BJP and Rajesh Verma of the BSP. Salim said Saxena's contentions are contrary to what one can see on the video-tape. The sources said Saxena conceded that his son's admission form submitted to a local college had been filled by him and the address as well as the telephone number stated in it were those of Amar Singh.

The issue would be discussed when the committee meets next, most likely on August 27.

The committee examined SP MP Reoti Raman Singh, who, according to the sources, admitted having gone to meet the three BJP MPs, but claimed that the issue under discussion was not the voting on the confidence motion but their admission to the SP. He said the amount mentioned in the tape was what one of the MPs said was necessary for running an SP unit once he switched sides.

Deo told The Indian Express that the committee had not taken any decision about summoning Amar Singh and Ahmed Patel, both members of the Rajya Sabha. The sources, however, said some members at the meeting contended that Amar Singh be called because one of the CDs with the probe panel was sourced by him. They said if the SP leader was not going to appear, there was no need to examine the CD. This matter too would be taken up at the next meeting.

The committee also recorded the evidence of Sudheendra Kulkarni, a former aide of L K Advani. Kulkarni, who had made a written submission to the committee on August 14 giving a detailed account of the tapping operation, handed a post-script to the panel. He alleged that CNN-IBN, in its telecast on August 11, had suppressed "important sections of the recorded material." The channel had not shown clips of Ahmed Patel's meetings with two BJP MPs at a five-star hotel, he said. Suhail Hindustani, who assisted him, had told him that a person in a yellow shirt, who carried the slush money, had accompanied Saxena to Amar Singh's house. This man, according to him, is seen near Argal's house in the telecast, but the channel has not shown him near Amar Singh's house, he added. "His identity and role must be properly probed," Kulkarni demanded.

Sources in the channel dismissed Kulkarni's claim. "He should check with BJP MPs who have themselves maintained that the so-called meeting at the hotel did not take place. When there is no footage, how can we show footage," they wondered.

Deo, when asked when the committee would submit its report, said, "as soon as possible." The extended deadline is August 29.

Heading: Raj, colleagues told to stay off Pune limits - Indian Express
Content:
The nationwide general strike called by Left trade unions on Wednesday may perhaps for the first time affect the functioning of the IT industry and special economic zones (SEZs) as the unions have decided not to spare them.

The sponsoring committee of trade unions on Monday said they had not exempted these sectors from the day-long shutdown against various policies of the UPA and would try to enforce the strike wherever they had strength.

While there are trade unions in several SEZs, notably the ones in Hyderabad and Chennai, the sunshine sector barring Left-ruled West Bengal is relatively free of unions.

CITU president M K Pandhe and AITUC general secretary Gurudas Dasgupta said the strike would be complete and claimed the support of workers' unions in key sectors like banking, insurance, defence, telecom, airports, railway besides central and state governments.

Significantly, though the ties between the DMK and Left parties have come under strain after the UPA-Left separation, DMK's trade union arm Labour Progressive Foundation (LPF) has extended its support to the strike.

Outfits like CITU, AITUC, HMS and UTUC have given the strike call, demanding strict implementation of labour laws, particularly in respect of minimum wages, working hours and social security and to protest the failure in tackling price rise and the Indo-US nuclear deal.

They are also demanding expansion of the scope of the Unorganised Workers' Bill, extension of the farm debt waiver scheme to provide relief to those who have taken loans from private moneylenders and lifting of the ban on government recruitments.

Heading: Amarnath the fuel, Advani Sankalp Yatra back on track - Indian Express
Content:
A day after they attacked the premises of a school, the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) was banned from public gatherings in the city. The police banned party chief Raj Thackeray and other activists from organising any meeting, gathering, discussion, agitation and media interaction in public or private places in the city till August 28.

Joint Commissioner of Police Rajendra Sonawane passed the order on Sunday and called it a preventive measure to maintain law and order in the city. Sonawane said Thackeray had instigated local youths against students from other states during his speech at Ganesh Kala Krida Kendra on August 14. Thackeray had told his party workers to count the number of students from other states on admission lists of various educational organisations and also demanded that private establishments display Marathi names on their premises. Sonawane said the ban was imposed because Thackeray was likely to visit the city and his statements might result in violent agitations causing loss of public and private property.

A group of MNS activists had attacked the Mercedes Benz International School in Hinjewadi for not hoisting the national flag on Independence Day. Following the incident, the city police had detained 64 MNS members from different parts of the city on Saturday as a preventive action.

Heading: Separatists’ march to UN office not a matter of concern: Govt - Indian Express
Content:
With the Amarnath row as the backdrop, the BJP's prime ministerial candidate L K Advani has decided to resume his Sankalp Yatra, which will include public rallies and mass contact programmes across the country. After a meeting of party office-bearers, BJP spokesperson Ravi Shankar Prasad said that while the yatra had to be abandoned due to rains, it was set to resume now in September.

"He'll address a whole range of issues, including terror, inflation, cash-for-votes scam, besides, of course, Amarnath," said BJP sources. Advani and BJP president Rajnath Singh will also address a rally of the Shri Amarnath Sangharsh Samiti (SASS) in Jammu on August 25, while a nationwide 'Jail Bharo' is planned for August 21 in solidarity with SASS.

At the meeting, the BJP asked its rank and file to look at the ongoing agitation in Jammu from the perspective of "Jammu and Kashmir". "We were getting feedback that a Jammu-Kashmir polarisation was taking shape on the ground. We have therefore decided to appeal to the nationalists in the Valley to help corner the separatists," said a BJP leader. The August 21 agitation too has thus been named "Jammu-Kashmir Bachao, Bharat Bachao" rally.

In another decision, the BJP has decided to identify the PDP — which it thinks is openly siding with the separatists and was instrumental in triggering the crisis — with the Congress.

"The party's 'Intellectual Cell' too will be organising talks and seminars across the country to build public opinion of the citizens against the injustice happening over the Amarnath issue," said Prasad.

The meeting decided to convene the BJP's three-day National Executive meet in Bangalore, beginning September 12. In another important policy decision, the BJP has decided to resume the process of candidate selection and will come out with its second list of candidates in the fist week of September. The BJP has decided to approach the Election Commission requesting for an extension of the deadline for enrollment of new names in the voters' list.

While Ananth Kumar and Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi would be coordinating Advani's yatra, Vinay Katiyar will be associated with the August 21 all-India stir. Bal Apte, Vijay Goel and Amitabh Sinha will be organising the countrywide seminars.

Heading: Volunteers form human chains to prevent clashes - Indian Express
Content:
The Centre on Monday sought to play down the significance of Kashmiri separatist leaders' march to UN office in Srinagar, saying nothing 'unusual' had taken place and stressed that such events did not undermine the Government's authority in the state.

"People keep submitting memoranda to the UN office both in Delhi and Srinagar. The Government has never stopped anyone from doing so," Home Secretary Madhukar Gupta told reporters.

"There is no question of any dilution in the authority of Government of India in Kashmir. The state of Jammu and Kashmir remains an integral part of India and there is no compromise on that," he said, when asked about waiving of Pakistani flags and anti-India slogan-shouting by the crowds in Srinagar.

"What's important is that the entire thing passed off peacefully," he said, adding that the Centre was keen to ensure that law and order situation was not disrupted.

A large number of people in Srinagar on Monday participated in a march to the UN office in the city and submitted a memorandum to the world body seeking its intervention in the current crisis in the state, precipitated by the transfer and subsequent withdrawal of forest land to the Amarnath Shrine Board for constructing temporary facilities for the pilgrims.

The Home Secretary also sought to debunk the theory of the separatist leaders that the Kashmir valley was under 'economic blockade' due to the protests in Jammu. Gupta said 480 trucks had travelled from Jammu to Srinagar since Sunday carrying supplies of essential items. In the same time, 530 trucks, including 415 carrying fruits meant for markets in the rest of the country, had reached Jammu from Srinagar.

Heading: Protestors court arrest across Jammu - Indian Express
Content:
As hundreds gathered at the Tourist Reception Centre (TRC) here for the march to the United Nations office on Monday, volunteers took it upon themselves to ensure that there were no clashes between angry protestors and the security forces.

After the Hurriyat Coordination Committee asked people to maintain discipline and peace during the rally at the TRC, they made human chains between the people and the police.

"This is a peaceful rally," said Bashir Ahmad Mir, a volunteer from Awantabhawan on the outskirts of Srinagar city. "We don't want bloodshed. We don't want to given them (security forces) any chance to open fire on people."

On Sunday, Srinagar's top police and civil administration had requested the Hurriyat leadership to shift the venue of the rally from the United Nations Military Observers' office to some other place. The request was made as Sonawar houses several sensitive security installations besides the Army cantonment and the residences of top mainstream leaders. The police feared that the mob could attack these installations and houses, leading to the loss of life and property. The Hurriyat leadership had assured the administration that the rally would be peaceful.

At Radio Kashmir that lies adjacent to the TRC ground, police and CRPF were deployed in high numbers and the road leading to Sonawar was closed. However, the volunteers formed their own security ring and didn't allow marchers to move close to the barricade.

"We believe in peaceful protests. They are more powerful," said a volunteer Adil Rashid. "We are against violence and our leaders have said it. We are here to ensure peace on the ground."

Such human chains to avoid a confrontation between security forces and people were visible throughout the city. Whenever a protest march moved close to a security bunker or installation, volunteers — mostly youths in their 20s — stepped in.

Heading: Cong warns Hurriyat against internationalising Amarnath row - Indian Express
Content:
Raising their pitch with demands to return the 800 kanals of land in Kashmir Himalayas to the Shri Amarnath Shrine Board (SASB), over one lakh people courted arrest across Jammu region on Monday.

While Shri Amarnath Sangharsh Samiti (SASS), which is spearheading the 48-day long agitation, said that nearly 3 lakh people had come to court arrest, the police put the number at over 77,000. An unprecedented number of protesters swarmed the city roads, which stood deserted early in the morning, and headed towards various police stations after 10 am, with men and women holding the Tricolour and chanting Bum Bum Bholey as they marched to court arrest.

The sight of the huge crowd virtually came as a shock to the police, who ran short of men and vehicles to take the protesters into custody. The police hurriedly arranged for SRTC buses to carry people to M A Stadium, schools, colleges and parks, which had been converted into temporary jails.

The protestors ransacked the office of the indoor sports complex, as there was no arrangement for drinking water in the stadium ground on a hot sunny day. They later took to the roads and pelted stones at SRTC buses, besides torching two temporary police booths in Dogra Chowk. Protestors also attacked the office of the People's Democratic Party in Gandhi Nagar but the police and CRPF personnel deployed there foiled their attempt to break into the office. The protestors also pelted stones at the NDTV office in nearby Shastri Nagar.

In Udhampur town, police had to lob teargas shells as a huge crowd instead of marching towards the District Police Lines, swarmed the local police station. Nearly half a dozen people were injured in police action. Later, senior police officers intervened and persuaded the protesters to leave the police station.

Heading: At Mira Road house of techie, family says he left in 2001 - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress on Monday warned the Hurriyat Conference and other separatist elements against internationalising the situation in Jammu and Kashmir, even as it equated the Hurriyat Conference and the Amarnath Sangharsh Samiti terming them as "two sides of the same coin". It also asked the BJP to rein in the Samiti.

Terming the Hurriyat-organised march to the UN office as "very unfortunate", the Congress said there was no such situation in the state which warranted a march to the UN office and denied that there was any human rights violation.

"We strongly condemn it and categorically say that any attempt to internationalise it will not be tolerated. If any person or political party or group has any grievances, then the Indian Constitution has so much flexibility that we could find some solution. J&K is an integral part of India and any international interference will not be tolerated at any cost," AICC spokesperson Manish Tewari said.

"So far as Amarnath Sangharsh Samiti is concerned, it is nothing else but a proxy of the RSS and the BJP. And the Sangharsh Samiti and the Hurriyat are two sides of the same coin. Both are trying to complicate an otherwise difficult situation," said Tewari. He said that the responsibility to "rein in" the Sangharsh Samiti rested squarely with the BJP.

Heading: ‘Recce’ of hospital during father’s treatment - Indian Express
Content:
The Ahmedabad blasts probe trail has led up to a flat on the sixth floor of a building on Mumbai's Mira Road. It is here that the family of Abdul Subhan Qureshi — who is accused of assembling the bombs as well as sending the terror e-mail — has been living since 2006.

At the flat, there is no response to the ringing of the doorbell. After a few minutes, the door opens an inch, revealing the burqa-clad face of Abdul's sister, who refuses to give her name but agrees to talk after a few questions. "We used to stay at Masjid Bunder earlier. Abdul had got into a quarrel with the family in the year 2001 and left the house and the family. Since then, we have not had any word from him, nor do we know as to how or where he has been staying," she says.

The family — including his mother, father, a few of his sisters as well as Abdul's wife and children — moved into this flat in Naya Nagar on Mira Road in 2006. Abdul and she are altogether nine siblings, she says.

Police say Qureshi alias Taufiq alias Tauqeer may have procured the explosives and timers for the Ahmedabad blasts as well as prepared the three e-mails announcing the role of the 'Indian Mujahideen' in the attacks. The Mumbai Police have also been trying to locate him after his name was allegedly revealed by some of the prime conspirators in the 7/11 serial train blasts.

Asked about the possibility of Abdul's involvement in the Ahmedabad blasts, the sister says: "According to the police, they are trying to trace a man named 'Tauqeer' alias Abdul Qureshi. However, we do not know for sure that he is our Abdul. Till we know the truth of the identity of the man sought by the police, we cannot really comment on it."

She adds that police officials have been visiting the family and asking about Abdul's whereabouts. "They have also taken a few of his belongings, including his laptop."

According to the Mumbai Police, following the train blasts two years ago, a massive manhunt was launched for Qureshi, a "highly active" SIMI member who is believed to have helped collect funds for the organisation as well as undergone training in explosives and bomb-making. However, Qureshi was never booked in the 7/11 case owing to insufficient evidence.

The Gujarat Police say Qureshi allegedly procured ammonium nitrate and timers for the Ahmedabad operation and attended SIMI meetings where the serial blasts were planned.

Records show that in 1999, he was arrested by the Kurla police in a case of defacement of property. He has never been booked by the ATS before under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act.

A senior ATS officer, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said that when SIMI national chief Safdar Nagori was arrested in Indore this year along with 12 other members, Qureshi was reported to have met him and left just an hour before the arrests.

"He has been on the run since 2001 and one of the reasons we have been unable to arrest him is that he never uses a cellphone or a fixed landline. No one can reach him. He only contacts members from public phones across the country," the officer said.

Heading: Police hunting other sleeper cell members - Indian Express
Content:
Imran Shaikh, one of the ten youths arrested by the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) for his alleged role in the July 26 Ahmedabad serial blasts, is said to have recced Ahmedabad Civil Hospital along with other conspirators when his father was undergoing treatment there.

Revealing this in a press release on Monday, the DCB officials said Imran's father, Ibrahim Sheikh, was a heart patient and being a BPL card holder, he had received free treatment at the U N Mehta Heart Hospital in Civil Hospital compound. He was admitted in hospital in March and April, 2008. He was again taken to the same hospital in June-end where stayed till July 9.

According to DCB officials, Imran, a resident of Vadodara, has confessed to have spent at least three nights in the Civil Hospital when he surveyed the hospital. His accomplices Yunus Mansuri, Usman Agarbattiwala, Zahid Shaikh and Samsuddin Shaikh, too, went around the hospital then on the pretext of visiting his father.

During the interrogation of the ten accused, the release added, it has also been found that like the terror training camps in Kerala and in Gujarat near Halol, many such camps were organised in states like Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka. These camps were attended by many SIMI activists from across the country, the release further added.

Heading: Blast mastermind’s photo released - Indian Express
Content:
After the recent arrests of three SIMI activists by the Mumbai Police Crime Branch and following the exposure of a sleeper cell of subversive elements in Pune by the state Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), the police are now on the lookout for a doctor believed to be an associate of the same group. According to sources, the suspect has been identified simply as 'Dr Noman'.

"There are some other members of the sleeper cell who are yet to be arrested. We have the names of these people. One person we are looking for is a SIMI activist named Dr Noman, who is actually a doctor by profession," Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria told The Indian Express.

Prior to the Gujarat Police's announcement that it had cracked the Ahmedabad blasts case, the ATS had arrested Nadeem Shaikh (27) and Ayaz Yusuf Khan (24) from Pune and booked them in a counterfeit currency case, while the Anti Extortion Cell of the Crime Branch arrested Bilal Gulam Rasool Kagzi from Gujarat in an extortion case.

"Nadeem, Ayaz and Bilal Kagzi, as well as one Imtiyaz Baba Mia Shaikh arrested in a dacoity case by the Thane (Rural) police, definitely have links with one another and we are probing whether they are linked to any extremist or terrorist acts. There is possibility of their involvement in terror activities but we have not yet found anything to link them to the Ahmedabad blasts," said Joint Commissioner of Police (ATS) Hemant Karkare.

The ATS has now secured permission from a court to conduct polygraph, brain-mapping and narco-analysis tests on Nadeem.

"We had filed an application in court and have been granted permission. The tests will be done some time in the middle of next week," said Karkare.

Both Nadeem and Kagzi are students of A K Khan Law College on the Pune-Sholapur Road. According to the police, a group of former and current students of the college were indoctrinated by one Yusuf Khan. Noman's name cropped up during Kagzi's interrogation. "Kagzi told us that he, along with three other youths, were indoctrinated by one Yusuf Khan in a mosque on the Pune-Sholapur Road some time in 2005-06. He told us that Noman attended these lectures," said Maria.

On Monday, Kagzi was subjected to a narco-analysis test at the Kalina Forensic Sciences Laboratory.

"Kagzi was present in Surat on the day of the blasts, and he is an important catch who could divulge important information on SIMI activities in Pune and even in Gujarat," said Maria.

Heading: Jaipur blasts: cleared by police, Infosys techie now wants job back - Indian Express
Content:
The DCB officials have released the photo of one of the two Ahmedabad blast masterminds, Abdul Subhan Usman Queshi alias Qasim alias Zaqir alias Kab alias Tauqir (Ansar) from Mira Road in Thane.

Qureshi allegedly planned the Ahmedabad blasts in association with one Qayamuddin, who is also absconding. Giving details of Qureshi who has worked as an editor and publisher of a Delhi-based monthly, Islamic Movement, the release added that he was wanted in at least five cases, including the Mumbai train blasts, in different parts of the country.

Heading: School suspends 350 students for skipping I-Day function - Indian Express
Content:
Picked up for questioning after the Jaipur blasts, Rashid Hussain, a senior network engineer with Infosys, lost his job. Though the police released him after nine days of detention, Rashid was sacked by his employer. The software engineer now wants his job back and is fighting the system that he says is "surgically targeting educated Muslims".

Although the police did not find anything substantial against him, two weeks after the release, Rashid was told to face an internal panel at Jaipur office of Infosys on June 23. The organisation maintained that he had furnished false work experience during the interview. "They did not mention the detention at all. This clearly shows they just wanted to get rid of me because of my religion," said Rashid. "I want to ask the Infosys authorities how they suddenly discovered that my documents were not in place. Had I not been picked up by the police, would they have fired me?"

Despite repeated attempts, spokesperson for Infosys Technologies could not be contacted.

Rashid was part of the Students' Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) before the organisation was banned. "This association with SIMI was the reason I was detained. I left SIMI because I had ideological differences with the organisation. This incident has led to character assassination of my entire family," he said.

Backed by human rights activists like Shabnam Hashmi, Rashid is in the city to talk to mediapersons about what he calls "re-victimisation" — first by police and then by society. "My career has been ruined because of the reckless manner in which the police behaved. I had been working with Infosys for three years and they never had a complaint against me. Despite being released, Infosys fired me without giving me any reason," he added.

Heading: Uttarakhand set to have a permanent capital - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 350 students of a private school in Indore, who skipped the Independence Day function to enjoy what they thought was the beginning of a mini-vacation, were punished with a longer, forced break on Monday.

The senior students of Imperial Academy School, located on Khandwa Road, were served a weeklong suspension for not attending the Independence Day function, mandatory for all students in the school.

When the students gathered for the morning assembly after a two-day break, including Raksha Bandhan holiday and Sunday, those who had attended the Friday's function in the school premises were asked to leave for classes, but not before the staff crosschecked their Friday attendance.

Barring a few students of Class I to Class V, all junior students had attended the function that included, besides flag hoisting and singing of the national anthem, a short cultural programme.

In a gathering of 1,473 students, 350 students of Class VI to XII were left to anticipate the likely punishment.

Some of them were made to come to the dais and speak a few lines on Independence Day and why it was important. "They could not go beyond a couple of lines," said chairperson of Malwa Education Society Dolly Luthra. "Some of them later admitted that they watched a recently released movie — Bachna Ae Haseeno. They had time to watch a three-hour film but not for a 40-minute mandatory function of national importance," she told The Indian Express on what prompted such a harsh action against the students.

The erring students were handed suspension letters within an hour and bundled into school buses that took them home. "They started calling up frantically and some of them arrived and gave apology letters," she said, adding that the idea was also to teach the parents a lesson.

The school calendar mentions that the attendance for August 15 and January 26 functions is mandatory. While the junior students were issued circulars last week, seniors were told that attendance was compulsory.

Some of the parents did express displeasure at the harsh punishment, but most seemed to have fallen in line. "More than 150 of them called up to apologise," the school PRO said.

The management has called a meeting at 2 pm on Tuesday when the society office-bearers would take a call on continuing the punishment. The school has taken disciplinary action against individuals but never en mass.

While all teachers had turned up, the school's DTP operator had a tough time explaining his absence when he arrived on Monday.

When he maintained that he had to take his wife to a hospital he was asked to go home and get the papers, which he did.

Heading: Booked for trying to ‘bribe judge’, Bansal quits - Indian Express
Content:
Uttarakhand is finally set to have a permanent capital almost eight years after it became a state. The one-member Justice Virender Dixit Commission, set up to demarcate a capital, has finally submitted its report to the state Government Justice Dixit, a retired Allahabad High Court judge, submitted the 250-page report to Chief Minister B C Khanduri on Sunday evening.

However, the contents of the report have not been made public yet.

Chairman of Uttarakhand media advisory council Dr Devender Bhasin told The Indian Express, "The Government will now study the report and will then decide on the future course of action."

The issue of choosing a capital for the state is politically very sensitive, as Dehradun continues to be the interim capital.

The Commission was set up on January 11, 2001, three months after the region achieved statehood. Since then, it was given ten extensions. After the deadline for the tenth term expired on July 31 this year, the Commission was granted an additional period of 17 days to finalise its report.

The Commission had also submitted an affidavit in the High Court that it would complete its work by August 17 in response to a PIL filed against the Commission's delay in deciding the permanent capital.

According to sources, the Commission considered four prominent areas, including Dehradun, Gair Sain, Ramnagar-Kashipur belt and the IDPL area in Rishikesh.

Both the BJP and the Congress want the report to be made public after a decision is taken on the public consent.

Heading: Lyngdoh suspension: 304 Congmen resign - Indian Express
Content:
Booked for attempting to bribe a high court judge, Additional Advocate General (Haryana) Sanjeev Bansal has resigned from his post. However, he continues to be missing, with the Chandigarh police unable to track him down.

Bansal tendered his resignation to the office of the Advocate General on August 16 on moral grounds, saying that since a case of corruption and criminal conspiracy had been registered against him, he would step down till he was cleared. The resignation has been forwarded to the Haryana Government by the Advocate General's office.

Bansal was booked on Saturday along with two others — his munshi Parkash Raj and Delhi-based businessman Ravinder Singh. Raj is reported to have carried Rs 15 lakh to the residence of Punjab and Haryana High Court Judge Nirmaljit Kaur on Wednesday night. An FIR was lodged after Kaur complained to the police. She also reported the matter to the Chief Justice.

Police said Singh had allegedly paid Bansal a huge amount to get a criminal case pending in the High Court settled. Earlier, Singh had claimed the amount was pertaining to a property deal he had struck with a resident of Panchkula. He said it was supposed to be delivered to one Nirmal Singh and was mistakenly sent to the judge's house. Preliminary investigation by the police, however, ruled out the possibility of the amount being related to any property deal.

While Bansal remains missing, Raj who is in police custody is reportedly not cooperating. Bansal has been handling several high-profile cases in the state. He was one of the dozen-odd Additional A-G's appointed by the Haryana Government about two years ago.

Heading: Riding the airwaves at 70 - Indian Express
Content:
In a major jolt to the state Congress, 304 workers resigned from the party on Monday in protest against the six-year suspension served on senior Congress leader and former home minister R G Lyngdoh by the Meghalaya Pradesh Congress Committee (MPCC).

In their resignation letter addressed to the Shillong City Congress president, the party workers said they were shocked by the MPCC's decision to suspend R G Lyngdoh for six years.

The letter signed by the 304 Congress members also said that Lyngdoh's suspension had "badly affected the party's image".

Lyngdoh, a senior Congress leader, also being seen as the future chief minister, was suspended from the party on June 3 after he told reporters that many Congress leaders were "power hungry and greedy". He had differences with many senior state Congress leaders, including former chief minister D D Lapang and some AICC members, on the way the party was being administered.

The MPCC served Lyngdoh a showcause notice for dubbing senior Congress leaders as "greedy", but the latter refused to reply. The MPCC then suspended him from the party for six years.

Lyngdoh's supporters in the party said that the six-year suspension was a "well calculated" move by the MPCC to deprive their leader of an opportunity to contest the 2009 Lok Sabha elections. They said that as "grassroots party workers" they will find it difficult to explain the Congress policy of "firing an honest and upright" leader like Lyngdoh.

The workers said their request to the party bosses to convene a meeting to discuss Lyngdoh's suspension was also ignored. They rued that the party leaders had "cheated and neglected" them and treated all of them in a "step-motherly" manner.

The members said that given such an attitude of the party, they had no option but to resign as primary members of the Congress.

Heading: Lecturer arrested for wife’s murder - Indian Express
Content:
Next time you tune into the FM and hear "Good Morning Shillong", don't pass the infectious voice greeting you as that of any other radio jockey. He is 70-year-old wisecrack Bah Besbha (Mr Best), the newest RJ in town, who is effortlessly stealing march over RJs quarter his age, both in energy and enthusiasm.

The station head of Sun FM, which was launched on Monday, Ian Khongmen, claims Besbha to be the "oldest RJ in the country" and his channel's USP.

The septuagenarian will be hosting the daily show called Besbha Show, which will be replete with wisecracks and messages for listeners.

With a vigour characteristic of teenagers, Besbha says: "I refuse to grow up anymore and feel like a James Bond in the midst of young girls who are my fellow RJs in the FM station."

Besbha, who was born in 1938, has seen radio ruling the airwaves, and then gradually making way for the television. He is now excited that the radio is back with a bang.

This former Director of Meghalaya Employment and Craftsmen Training says, " My family was initially bewildered when I told them I will be working as a RJ. They thought it was an in-thing for the younger generation." However, it took them only sometime to appreciate my decision, he added.

Besbha, a regular in the local television comedy programmes, admitted he did doubt whether he was cut out for the job. "But when I grabbed the microphone and spoke into it, all my doubts disappeared."

Author of a number of books in Khasi, Besbha will conduct the show in that language. "I will do the show in Khasi as I want to promote the language among the younger generation."

Heading: In Kerala’s land-industrialisation tussle, CPM overrides CM - Indian Express
Content: Seven months after a teacher, Swagata Choudhury, died after falling on the railway track at Daton Station in West Bengal, her lecturer husband, Pinak Choudhury, was arrested on Sunday for allegedly murdering her. Pinak had said that he along with Swagata (40), a teacher at Jail Road Boys Secondary School in Shillong, and their daughter, were returning from Puri on the Puri Express. Swagata, he had said, fell on the track while trying to board the moving train. She had gotten off the train to chase a thief who had snatched her bag. Swagata's family, however, suspected foul play and lodged a complaint against Pinak.

Heading: Dantewada awaits its first helping of Indiamix - Indian Express
Content:
The CPI(M) giving a burial to the proposed second edition of land reforms in Kerala, in favour of industrialisation, prompted Chief Minister V S Achuthanandan to comment on Saturday that "the boom in the real estate market cannot be reckoned as the yardstick for development".

In Kerala, land had attained an unexpected premium with the emergence of real estate developers and land bank mafia. Trading in agricultural land had become a lucrative business. VS had always wanted to take on the real estate mafia and had locked horns with rivals in the party over this issue.

He had mooted second land reforms last year, when his government wrested back thousands of acres of revenue land across Kerala, especially in the high ranges of Idukki district, where several resorts were demolished.

However, much to his chagrin, the idea was spiked by the CPI(M) and CPI.

While symbolically taking back a tract of estate owed by Tata Tea in Idukki, VS had declared that Kerala would go for another round of land reforms, in which the land taken back from the encroachers would be distributed among the landless agricultural workers and other backward segments. He had made the declaration when stakes in land were high for a wide spectrum of interest groups — estate owners, real estate mafia, Dalits who were agitating for land.

As expected, the CM's declaration was echoed by the Dalits in a different manner. People belonging to the lower economic and social strata had encroached upon several estates, whose lease agreements had expired.

One such agitation has been going on at Chengara in central Kerala since August 4, 2007. Around 3,000 families have erected dwellings in a rubber plantation owned by Harrison Malayalam Plantations Limited. Their argument: the lease period of the estate is over and hence, it should be distributed among the landless.

Stray incidents of similar encroachments had been reported from elsewhere in the state. But many movements lost steam midway for want of support from mainstream political parties. In fact, the agitation being staged at Harrison's estate has been facing opposition from all political parties.

The CPI(M)'s decision to jettison the second round of land reforms stemmed from the realisation that such a move would hamper industrialisation of the state. Besides, that move would only rattle the social fabric in Kerala by spurring the agricultural workers to take on the upper class farmers. While closing the file of second land reforms, the party took a pragmatic approach on the larger estates whose lease period was over. "We would look into each case individually. All estates need not be taken back. But the lease agreement could be renewed with a steep hike in the lease rent," said a party leader.

The party decision, overriding VS's dream, is creating ripples among the basic class. "The Dalits constitute the mass base of Left parties. The CPI(M)'s decision to drop land reforms at this stage is a matter of worry for the backward communities. The move would have political repercussions," said M Geethanandan, co-ordinator for tribal land movements. He said during the first land reforms, which began in 1957, agricultural workers and other backward groups had got nothing and were looking forward to the second one.

The Reform Story

•The land reforms were introduced in Kerala by the first communist ministry in 1957 to ensure land to the tiller. As per Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963, a ceiling of land area was fixed for individuals and joint families as 15 acres. Individuals were prevented from owning, holding, possessing land in excess of the ceiling area, with effect from January 1970. The purpose of the Act was to redistribute land to agricultural workers and to reduce the average size of the land holdings to less than 0.4 hectare with 90 per cent holdings being less than half a hectare in size. Plantation crops were exempted from the purview of the Act. About 32 lakh families benefitted from the re-distribution of land.

Heading: With Mamata firm on agitation, Nano may miss deadline - Indian Express
Content:
Clearing the initial bureaucratic red-tape and procedural delays, an ambitious scheme aimed at making "fortified blended food" available to children, pregnant and lactating mothers of Dantewada district in south Bastar, appears to be finally taking shape. In January this year, Union Steel Minister Ram Vilas Paswan formally launched the Grameen Pushti Yojana. The project, funded by public sector National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC), was scheduled to take off by March. However, the scheme hit a roadblock following a series of objections raised by NMDC officials over its funding.

The NMDC, which operates major mechanised iron ore mines at Bailadila in Bastar, had come up with this social development project to be implemented in partnership with United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), to make available fortified blended food called "Indiamix", containing wheat, soya, vitamins and minerals, to the vulnerable population.

Launching the scheme at a function in Bastar — hotbed of Maoist violence in the state — Paswan distributed 15 bags of "Indiamix", after a verbal understanding between the NMDC and the WFP that other modalities for implementation of the scheme would be soon worked out.

According to NMDC sources in Bastar, the proposal was to provide nutritious food to 31,000 children in the age group of six months to six years through Anganwadis for a period of five years. Its cost worked out to be around Rs 2 crore per annum. Similarly, 49,000 others, including adolescent girls, pregnant women and lactating mothers, were to be given "fortified blended food" at an estimated cost of Rs 4.33 crore per annum.

Sources said NMDC's finance department raised a volley of queries when it came to placing funds to the tune of Rs 6 crore with WFP, the world's largest humanitarian agency providing food aid to 100 million people in 80 countries every year.

The related file moved up and down at NMDC headquarters in Hyderabad during the last seven months and finally the issue came up before the Board of Directors, which gave its approval on July 24 to release Rs 2 crore for implementation of the scheme.

When contacted, NMDC's deputy general manager (corporate social responsibility) S R Bandhkavi said that the public sector undertaking was committed to implement the scheme to provide fortified food to the locals in Dantewada. "Being a government organisation, certain set of procedures have to be followed before placing funds with any agency. There have been some procedural delays. WFP is not registered in India. Hence, the company would not get income tax benefit under Section 80-C," he said, adding that it has now been agreed that WFP would register a trust within six months. Meanwhile, the NMDC has decided to release half of the amount so as to start the scheme as early as possible, Bandhkavi said.

J K Raman, head, resource mobilisation, United Nations World Food Programme, said over telephone, "It's a new project and it could take some time. A tripartite agreement, to be signed between NMDC, United Nations World Food Programme and Chhattisgarh Government, is ready."

Pointing out that the WFP has initiated a process of establishing a trust, comprising prominent personalities, he said it could help sort out many issues, including the one related to tax exemption to companies coming forward to contribute towards such a cause. He added that United Nations World Food Programme plans to set up a field office in Bastar — either in Dantewada or at Jagdalpur — to ensure smooth implementation of the five-year-long project. He said the state Government has to play an important role in implementation of such projects as the existing infrastructure, such as Anganwadis, have to be used to reach out to the beneficiaries.

Heading: Last excuse gone, time to act for parties - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee's plan for an indefinite blockade at the Singur plant of Tata Motors from August 24 has generated serious concerns among the industry and business lobby here.

Right now, Tata Motors is racing against time to meet the October deadline for Nano. Should Mamata insist on a showdown, the company's time frame may go haywire. Industrialists say that this would reflect badly on the overall business environment in West Bengal and as a result, not only the Tatas, others would suffer too.

The state Government, the industry, and Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee have all, in the past weeks, made repeated appeals to Mamata to sort out differences through negotiation and not upset the progress of the plant which might jeopardise the interests of the state. On Monday, the CM invited her for talks and again stressed the importance of the project for the state.

The industry is also trying to put an indirect pressure on her. On August 19, it will be a rare occasion, when responding to the invitation from several chambers of commerce — representing a cross section of industry in Bengal — Mamata will participate in an interactive session.

The Trinamool chief, however, is in no mood to let go of the land issue with Lok Sabha elections round the corner. Her party's Singur Krishi Jami Raksha Committee is preparing for a show of strength with 200,000 people and 21 points of blockade along the Tata Motors plant. Mamata is demanding that Tata and the state Government return 400 acres of land for which farmers have not taken their compensation. This land, she claims, the company has in excess of its requirement.

"We will organise a peaceful agitation near the plant. It will be a continuous agitation. It is the state Government which is inciting violence. Recently, the state Home Secretary went to Singur and said that he will arrest farmers," she said, when asked whether the agitation would be peaceful or not.

Her party has constructed 21 makeshift stages across the boundary wall of the Tata Motors site and along the Durgapur Expressway. "We are expecting 200,000 supporters to turn up from different districts, apart from the farmers of Singur," said Becharam Manna, convenor of Singur Save Farmland Committee. Members of the Committee said there are chances of people storming the project site during the agitation, "If people get emotional, what can we do? We can only request them to show restraint. If the police use force, we will not sit idle," said Manna. The party plans to block workers from entering the site, thus thwarting the project work.

Last week, the TMC and Save Farmland Committee organised a number of meetings in Singur and other districts to garner support for the agitation. The party is bullish because of its success in Singur in the recent panchayat elections.

Out of the 16 village panchayats in Singur, TMC has won 15. In the last elections it had won only four. It has also increased its tally from 12 seats, last time, to 37 in panchayat samitis. The party has won all the three zilla parishad seats in Singur. Naturally, it is time for Mamata and her supporters to flex some muscles.

Meanwhile, officials working at the Tata plant fear that hundreds of daily labourers might flee the site and that would slowdown the work and would pose a serious problem. Apart from a sustained agitation, the TMC-led panchayat samiti is likely to stop giving out licenses to the ancillary units, which would further create problems for the functioning of the plant. According to officials at the plant, the company may bring in components from outside, if the ancillary plant is not ready within the given time frame.

On July 29, members of the Singur Krishi Jami Raksha Committee beat up an engineer of the construction agency. Violence and intimidation also drove out a number of workers from the plant site.

"Two weeks back only 40 per cent of the workers were available at the plant, following disturbances. Last week, the attendance jumped to 65 per cent. We are holding regular meetings to review the security situation," said Prasenjit Chattopadhyay, BDO of Singur and a member of the state Government's monitoring team.

The local CPI(M) leaders, backing the project, are hopeful that Nano will meet its deadline, but are not so sure whether the entire project will be ready by October. "Tata's mother plant will be ready, considering the current pace of work, but the entire project may not meet the deadline. The ancillary units are yet to pick up," said Dibakar Das, district CPI(M) leader.

"According to Tata Motors' report, submitted to us last week, 75 per cent of the work is over. With the current pace they are expected to meet the October deadline, provided there is no disruptions inside the plant. But there are problems pertaining to the ancillary units. Out of the 35 which were given licences, 17 are in various stages of construction. We do not expect them to start operating on time and be ready for the October-November deadline," said the BDO. "The work for engine shop, paint shop is complete. There are six big shades which are also complete," he added.

The state Government and plant authorities are gearing up for August 24 agitation. Following the on-the-spot assessment by the state Home Secretary, Ashok Mohan Chakrabarti, and the state Director General of police, A B Vohra, security inside and around the 997.11 acres plant has been upgraded. Armed policemen and RAF personnel are manning the entry points and guarding the periphery wall of the plant. The local administration and plant authorities also plan to arrange for the stay of the labourers inside the site so that they are not harassed during the agitation.

Nano: Progress Report Card

•75% of the work complete

• Work on engine shop, paint shop, six big shades complete

• Approach ways into the plant from its five gates complete

• Effluent treatment plant being set up

• Roads inside the plant almost complete

• 55 ancillary units have been allotted land

• 35 ancillary units have been given licences

• 17 ancillary units in various stages of construction

Source: Prasenjit Chattopadhyay, BDO of Singur

Heading: Watchful India says Pak army holds key - Indian Express
Content:
The immediate reaction in Pakistan's corridors of power and streets to the resignation of President Pervez Musharraf was one of optimism and opportunity.

"His resignation will bring stability hopefully," said Foreign Minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi. He noted that the stock market, which had suffered in recent sessions, had reacted positively.

Aitzaz Ahsan, the leader of a lawyers' movement that has been pushing for Musharraf's ouster and the reinstatement of 57 dismissed judges, said the resignation was a cause "to rejoice".

The governing coalition that engineered the ouster of Musharraf must now face a range of potential problems, minus the main factor that unified it — opposing him.

Zardari and Sharif will have to reach an agreement on the choice for the next President. So far, there are few clues about the contenders.

A more immediate challenge is the judiciary, which Musharraf tried to weaken over its opposition to his rule as both Pakistan's military and civilian leader. Sharif has insisted on the reinstatement of the 57 Supreme and high court judges, including Chief Justice Iftikhar Muhammad Chaudhry, after their dismissal under emergency rule last November. But Zardari holds that judges appointed during the emergency should also be retained.

Beyond that, the coalition will now hold sole responsibility to cope with a deteriorating economy and the continued threat from a resurgent Taliban. Musharraf lost popular support in Pakistan over efforts to contain the Taliban that were seen as appeasement toward the US.

"I think the political leaders have no excuse now," said Rasul Baksh Rais, a political analyst who teaches political studies at Lahore University of Management Sciences. "They have to address the immediate issues like inflation and the long-term structural problems of Pakistani polity. They can't use Musharraf as an excuse any more."

Rais said that the departure of Musharraf was a "great moment and a great change".

Since the general election in February, which brought the coalition to power, Pakistan had been in political limbo, he said, neither fully governed by the Parliament nor by the president, with the two sides in constant conflict. This led to paralysis during which little was achieved and the economy faltered, he said.

The announcement of plans to impeach Musharraf this month united a wide spectrum of Pakistani society. After his resignation on Monday, the country looked toward its future.

"Now, we can expect more normal politics," said Nasim Zehra, a political analyst based in Islamabad. "Politics are inherently competitive, but the ruling-coalition partners are likely to stay together for a while."

Chorus from west Good friend...Pak future is the key

•"We will continue to work with the Pak government and political leaders, urge them to redouble their focus on Pakistan's future and its most urgent needs, including stemming extremism. (Musharraf) has been a friend to the US and one of the world's most committed partners in war against terrorism, extremism."

CONDOLEEZZA RICE, US Secretary of State

•"During Musharraf's time we have seen a deepening of UK-Pak relations. We wish him well in the future. But relations between the UK and Pakistan don't depend on individuals... we support measures that promote strong democratic institutions which lead to stability in Pakistan. "

GORDON BROWN, Spokesman for British PM

•"What kind of changes does this bring to the "war-on-terror" and the Afghan situation? I don't expect any significant change for now. It is not a time for us to make predictions."

YASUO FUKUDA, Japanese PM

•"We would like the next president and the Pak government to work together with respect for the institutions to address the many challenges facing Pakistan. "French Foreign Secretary

• "Russia hopes the resignation (of Musharraf) will have no negative consequences for political stability. And the situation will not leave the limits of the constitutional framework.

Russian Foreign Secretary

Heading: Musharraf’s 9 years of walking the tightrope - Indian Express
Content:
As Pervez Musharraf stepped down as the President of Pakistan, a cautious New Delhi offered a stoic "no comment-it's-an-internal-matter-of-Pakistan" routine, but Pakistan-watchers expressed concerns that the Pakistan Army may end up calling the shots. They said the onus is now on the US and Europe to support the Government vis-à-vis the Pakistan Army.

Former Indian diplomats and experts, who dealt with Musharraf and watched him closely in the last 10 years, said that with him stepping down, the buffer between the Pakistan's political class and the powerful Army is gone.

Though most of them did not celebrate his exit, some "welcomed" the development with a note of caution.

Brajesh Mishra, who was the National Security Advisor during the NDA regime and had worked closely with Musharraf's Pakistan, welcomed the development, but put a cautionary note as he said: "It is obvious that US and Europeans played a role in Musharraf's exit, now it is their responsibility as huge donors to Pakistan Army to support the civilian control of the armed forces. This is absolutely necessary to guarantee for democracy in Pakistan to survive."

K Subrahmanyam, eminent strategic affairs expert who headed the Kargil review committee, said: "There appears to be a link between Musharraf's decline and increase in activities on the Indo-Pak border and terror activities inside India. He has been made a fall guy by the Army and his departure means losing a buffer between the political and the military establishment."

Former Indian High Commissioner to Pakistan, G Parthasarathy, who was in Islamabad in 1999, said: "The new civilian President will not carry any authority with the Army, even though he or she will be a member of the National Security Council. So, with a weak Government in place, be it on India or Afghanistan or nuclear weapons, General Kayani will be the real ruler." Both Parthasarathy and Subrahmanyam cited instances of increased ceasfire violations — Defence Minister A K Anthony had recently said there were 19 violations this year — to press home their point.

While Subrahmanyam said: "The Pakistan Army will still maintain its role and it", Parthasarathy cited the recent failed bid by the civilian Government to wrest control over the ISI.

Former external affairs minister K Natwar Singh said: "What I am worried is that whether the civilian Government will be able to tackle terrorism. And whoever becomes the new President of Pakistan, how is he going to tackle the rogue elements in the Pakistan Army."

Heading: Delhi hopes for best, prepares for worst - Indian Express
Content:
A man of often impetuous decisions, Pervez Musharraf reversed position after 9/11 and joined the United States, becoming one of Washington's most crucial allies in the campaign against terrorism.

It was a bold stroke that boosted the Bush administration in its immediate war against al-Qaeda and the Taliban in Afghanistan, and allowed the US to work with Pakistani intelligence to arrest senior Qaeda operatives inside Pakistan. Musharraf also gave Washington permission to strike at Qaeda targets in his nation's lawless tribal areas.

But the assurances turned out to be less than promised, and though Musharraf forged a personal bond with President Bush, he proved to be a tough, frustrating customer for the US.

Pakistan's powerful ISI agency never severed ties with the Taliban. Nine years later, the Taliban is putting up a ferocious fight against the US in Afghanistan, and is providing shelter to al-Qaeda in the tribal areas.

"Musharraf continued to provide cover to the Taliban, but still managed to convince the Americans for many years that it was not a double game," said Ahmed Rashid, a Pakistani expert on the Taliban and the author of Descent into Chaos, a book that details the relationship between Musharraf and Washington. "It was a remarkable feat of balancing on the tightrope."

The feat was so skilful that Musharraf won more than $10 billion in US military assistance for his army.

About half the military aid was supposed to be spent on bolstering the counterinsurgency skills of the Pakistani Army. Much of that money never reached the military and was allocated instead to Pakistan's general budget, but Bush was so anxious to keep Musharraf as an ally it chose not to complain.

Washington finally lost patience. In a diplomatic showdown, the Pentagon and the CIA confronted Prime Minister Yousaf Raza Gilani with evidence that the Pakistani intelligence service helped plan the July 7 terror attack against the Indian Embassy in Afghanistan's capital, Kabul.

By that time, Musharraf's power was eclipsed, and the Bush administration acknowledged that Musharraf's usefulness was past.

After grabbing power from Nawaz Sharif in October 1999, Musharraf had begun his tenure as President with a wave of support from a public weary of a decade of weak and corrupt civilian Government.

In the beginning, he attracted competent people to his Cabinet, and promised to tackle longstanding problems, including the spread of madrasas, religious schools that had turned into breeding grounds of Islamic extremists.

But the madrasas remained untouched, mainly because Musharraf handed the task to the Ministry of Religious Affairs which was opposed to the plan, according to Jehangir Tareen, a former minister of industries and special projects in the Musharraf Cabinet.

Musharraf backed some important reforms in the news media and the rights of women, say his supporters.

One of his greatest shortcomings, Tareen said, was his disdain of democratic methods, and civilian politicians.

When Bhutto was assassinated in December last year, her husband Asif Ali Zardari picked up the reins of the PPP and formed an uneasy coalition with the PML(N) that left Musharraf's political party flailing for support.

His failure to manage his double game of keeping the Americans on his side and keep allowing the religious extremists to thrive may have proved his undoing, and left Pakistan in a more precarious position, Rashid said.

Heading: Geelani says ‘good riddance’, but for Valley, Musharraf was a friend - Indian Express
Content:
•Was New Delhi prepared for this?

Well, it wasn't surprised. Musharraf's fall was imminent the day he decided to give up Army Chief's job. India's assessment: he would weaken, authority would be fragmented. So it maintained contact with all political parties and in May when Pranab Mukherjee visited Pak after elections, he met Nawaz Sharif and Asif Zardari. The two Prime Ministers also met in Colombo earlier this month. In China for the Olympics opening ceremony, Sonia met Bhutto's son Bilawal.

•Will Musharraf's exit change the New Delhi-Islamabad engagement?

Too early to say but one thing clear: too many uncertainties. Few know how the ruling coalition can impact Army and ISI which control Pak attitudes on Kashmir, Afghanistan and terror. First signs of drift are there: Kabul Embassy attack, resurgent Taliban, LoC incidents. Don't expect rapid forward movement on tricky issues.

•What happens to mechanisms put in place as part of the peace process?

These will continue and there are so many pending proposals that both sides have enough work on their table for a while. Delhi will continue with engagement and would, in fact, show added commitment to foster stronger ties with the new leadership in Islamabad.

•Nawaz and Zardari are distancing themselves from the US. What does it mean?

They have a political compulsion to do so and Delhi understands that. On critical issues, India hopes US can prevail. Particularly, when it comes to strengthening political control over the Army, the ISI, security of its nuclear weapons.

•What should Delhi be wary of?

Coalition partners Nawaz and Zardari aren't exactly the best of friends. Opposition to Musharraf brought them together and now that he's gone, expect conflict, instability. The unexpected means that bilateral relationship might be swayed by sentiments, triggered by circumstances and events: a terror attack or military adventurism. India's best hope: Pak leadership consolidates, US remains entrenched to influence events. But Delhi takes heart in the fact that there is a constitutional system — rather than a dominant individual — in place.

Heading: Towards end, Musharraf very cooperative: Azad - Indian Express
Content:
Pervez Musharraf's resignation on Monday exposed the faultlines in the newly minted alliance between the Hurriyat factions in the Valley. While hawk Syed Ali Shah Geelani announced the resignation to a massive gathering of protestors as a "good news" — saying the "Pakistani General" who had damaged the cause of Pakistan, harmed the Islamic nation and destroyed the Kashmir cause to save his chair was gone — moderate Mirwaiz Umer Farooq sitting besides him looked far from amused.

More so as Geelani rubbed it in that the former Pakistan president had played favourites with the Kashmiri separatist leadership. "Musharraf when he had power made his own leaders in Kashmir," Geelani, who was sidestepped by the former General in his peace process with New Delhi, told the crowd.

"Musharraf, the enemy of Islam, who waged war against his own people at America's behest, has resigned. Hear the good news," Geelani said, to a roar from a section of the gathering.

However, while the Hurriyat hardliner may have no love lost for the outgoing Pakistani president, Musharraf was widely admired in the Valley. Apart from Mirwaiz, whom he roped in to consolidate his peace initiatives with India, Musharraf had over the years extended his sphere of influence across the Valley's mainstream leadership. He met National Conference leader Omar Abdullah and even some PDP leaders on their visit to Pakistan.

It was Mirwaiz though who was his darling, making the Hurriyat chairman the consensus separatist with both Islamabad and New Delhi.

Mirwaiz, on his part, became Musharraf's ardent advocate in Kashmir and played along with his flexible settlement options for the state. He supported Musharraf's four-point proposals, which for some time almost looked to have settled the question.

Looking back, Mirwaiz still rues the lost opportunity. "Yes, Musharraf made some bold gestures on Kashmir. But there was no response from New Delhi. The drift has taken us back to the beginning now," he said.

At the same time, Mirwaiz said he saw no fundamental conflict between the policies of Musharraf and the new coalition government. "In fact, Nawaz Sharif is the first Pakistani leader who took steps for a settlement of Kashmir in 1999," Mirwaiz said. "Similarly the late Benazir Bhutto had also expressed herself in support of the Musharraf's initiatives. We will try to pick up the threads from where we left them."

The mainstream NC and PDP have also been Musharraf admirers. For Omar Abdullah, Musharraf represented "a rare window of opportunity missed by New Delhi" and for Mehbooba Mufti, his proposals with a few variations could have led the way.

After Musharraf's exit, there is a big question mark on how Islamabad will handle the separatists in the Valley. More so when secessionist sentiments are again running high in the state. From the looks of it, the new Pakistan dispensation has so far refused to play favourites.

While Geelani is well-regarded among some sections of the new dispensation, other mainstream leaders don't fare too badly. The Valley still remembers how Omar and Mehbooba were feted on their recent visits to the neighbouring country.

Heading: Prachanda sworn in as PM of Nepal - Indian Express
Content: Former J&K CM Ghulam Nabi Azad said on Monday that Musharraf had been very "cooperative" towards the latter part of his tenure and hoped that the new government would pursue his policies. "In the latter part of his tenure, he was conciliatory and wanted peace and harmony. He wanted to settle the dispute through dialogue and mutual cooperation. We hope the new government pursues the same path," Azad told The Indian Express. He also accused Pakistan of reluctance to open the cross-LoC trade route, one of the key demands of the Hurriyat.

Heading: Nobel laureate Ebadi sues agency for daughter report - Indian Express
Content:
Pushpakamal Dahal Prachanda was sworn in on Monday as the first Prime Minister of Republic Nepal, but he failed to form a full size Cabinet as planned following dispute over possession of key portfolios among the two major coalition partners — Communist Party of Nepal-Unified Marxist Leninist (CPN-UML) and the Madheshi Janadhikar Forum (MJF).

President Rambaran Yadav administered oath of office and secrecy to Prachanda on Monday, but the Cabinet formation has been put off as coalition partners were still holding parleys. The MJF, the third largest party in the cabinet, staked its claim on Foreign Affairs and Communication, although both had been allocated to the UML in the preliminary round of discussions with the Maoists last week.

The Prime Minister would be visiting Beijing on Saturday to participate in the closing ceremony of the Olympic Games. His Indian counterpart Manmohan Singh has already invited Prachanda to be his guest "at your earliest convenience".

Prachanda also invited direct confrontation with the Nepal Army as the Communist Party of Nepal-Maoists (CPN-M) backed out of its earlier decision that the National Army will be deployed for the security of the Prime Minister's office. Instead, the party decided that the People's Liberation Army (PLA) would be in the first ring of the multi-layer security set-up.

"Prachanda is the supreme commander of both PLA and the Nepal Army and both should be involved in the security set-up," Netra Bikram Chanda alias Biplab, a powerful leader of the CPN-M said.

The Maoist attitude towards the Nepal Army also drew sharp reaction from the MJF. The party's Central Committee member Sharad Singh Bhandary said that the CPN-M was and provoking retaliation from the army.

PLA leader Rambahadur Thapa 'Badal', likely to be inducted as the Defence Minister, will be in charge of the Nepal Army, indicating that he had limited choice—either to follow dictate or defy.

The CPN-M secretariat also decided that senior leaders of the party would be joining the Cabinet. There are indications that Baburam Bhattarai would be taking over as Finance Minister.

Prachanda also broke from the tradition of taking oath in Nepal's national dress — Daura Suruwal — as he chose to wear suit. He also refused to take the prescribed oath "in the name of truth or God", and instead took the oath in the name of the 'people', something his political rivals plan to challenge in Supreme Court.

Heading: US worried, Russia says pullout on - Indian Express
Content:
Nobel laureate Shirin Ebadi says she's filed a lawsuit against Iran's official news agency because of an incorrect report that her daughter converted from Islam. Ebadi said Monday she's taking IRNA to court for "spreading lies and insults".

Last month, IRNA reported that Ebadi's daughter converted to the Bahai faith — which is not recognised in Iran — to earn Bahai support for her mother's humanitarian work. Ebadi and her daughter, Narges Tavassolian, deny the report and say they're both Shiite Muslims, the majority faith in Iran.

Ebadi is a lawyer, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2003 for her work advocating greater rights for women and children in Iran. She's scheduled to defend seven Bahai leaders arrested in May for allegedly endangering Iran's national security.

Heading: Met police chief ‘bugged’ Asian officer - Indian Express
Content:
Moscow said it had begun a military pullback from Georgia on Monday and President Dmitry Medvedev promised a "crushing response" to any future attack on Russian citizens.

The White House urged a Russian withdrawal "without delay", the latest in a series of similar appeals, which have had no visible impact as Moscow has declined to set a pullout timetable.

A senior US official said there were no signs yet that the Russian forces had begun to leave. Georgia said they were broadening their presence.

"Quite the opposite. They are spreading out to other regions," Deputy Foreign Minister Giga Bokeria said.

In a show of defiance, Medvedev said: "If anyone thinks that they can kill our citizens and escape unpunished, we will never allow this."

"If anyone tries this again, we will come out with a crushing response. We have all the necessary resources, political, economic and military," a stern-looking Medvedev told World War Two veterans in the Russian city of Kursk.

He then flew to Vladikavkaz, near the border of the conflict zone of South Ossetia, to hand out medals to soldiers who took part in the operation.

In Moscow, the Russian General Staff told a briefing that Russian troops had begun their pullout from the conflict zone, though there was no independent verification of this.

"I can say for certain when the New Year will come, but I cannot give an exact date for the withdrawal of our troops from the conflict area yet," said Col-General Anatoly Nogovitsyn.

Russian commanders accused Georgia of wrecking a planned prisoner exchange and continuing to mount isolated sniper and sabotage attacks on its positions.

The 10-day confrontation around South Ossetia has killed more than 170 Georgians, dealt a blow to the Georgian military, damaged the country's economy and disrupted road and rail links.

Heading: It’s a dictator’s life - Indian Express
Content:
Britain's most senior police officer of Asian origin was illegally bugged and put under surveillance on the orders of the Metropolitan police chief, leaked Scotland Yard documents have revealed.

According to the papers, over 300 telephone calls of Assistant Commissioner Tarique Ghaffur were tapped in an elaborate operation overseen directly by Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sir Ian Blair, The Daily Telegraph reported. Ghaffur was also photographed at more than 30 meetings with another officer at restaurants and cafes in London in the operation codenamed 'Helios'.

The "bugging" claims surfaced as the Asian officer's lawyers prepare this week to announce formal legal proceedings for racial discrimination against Sir Ian, who was placed under formal investigation by the UK Home Office this month. "AC Ghaffur was the subject of direct surveillance and given a pseudo name (Vivaldi). This was a direct attack on his honesty and integrity," claim the documents prepared by Ghaffur's lawyers.

Heading: Musharraf Falling - Indian Express
Content:
Pervez Musharraf dominated Pakistan after taking power in a high-altitude coup nearly nine years ago and led a reluctant Islamic nation into the US-led war on terror — a step that earned him plaudits in the West but hatred at home.

Although Musharraf's decision to side with Washington after the Sept 11 attacks helped rescue Pakistan from the status of a pariah nation, it was followed by an explosion in Islamic militancy at home. Combined with his fumbled efforts to stay in power as democracy returned to Pakistan, he leaves the presidency reviled by many of his countrymen.

His demise was as tortured as his arrival was swift.

Musharraf, an urbane special forces veteran, seized power in a 1999 coup from then-prime minister, Nawaz Sharif.
