India has said it's willing to be accommodative to concerns raised by some members as long as these are reflected in a way that seeks India's partnership to further the cause of non-proliferation rather than an intrusive approach to "discipline" by way of periodic review or, for that matter, draw commitments on CTBT.

India has told the US and NSG members that while it held a principled opposition to the NPT because of its discriminatory approach, it never abandoned the idea of complete non-proliferation. And that there many areas in which it can work with the NSG on this. So several ideas are being explored, including a continuous dialogue or a long-term partnership where India is treated as a partner and not like a potential violator. New Delhi wants the language of the exemption to clearly reflect this approach.

On certain NSG countries suggesting a ban on transfer of enrichment and reprocessing technology, India's view is that there is no consensus in the group itself on this and, therefore, to take a decision just for India will be "discriminatory". This view is endorsed by Russia and France, said sources.

Heading: Rice says India deal above pact with Russia - Indian Express
Content:
The death of two people while making a bomb in Kanpur on Sunday has prompted the Centre to write to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati suggesting that the state Government seek a CBI probe into the matter.

Minister of State for Home Sriprakash Jaiswal, who represents Kanpur constituency in the Lok Sabha, told reporters on Tuesday that he had learnt "from his sources" that the two people belonged to the Bajrang Dal, "an objectionable organisation". "I have written to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister that if the state Government so decides, a CBI probe can be initiated into the matter," Jaiswal said. He said police had recovered seven more bombs as well as some more material used for making explosives from the site of the explosion.

"There is a distinct possibility that this might unearth some plan to carry out terror attacks. The links can be spread in other states too. The UP Police therefore might not be able to get to the root of such a plan on its own," Jaiswal said.

In his letter to Mayawati, Jaiswal did not take the name of Bajrang Dal, describing it just as an "extremist" organisation. The letter comes just a day after the Supreme Court extended the ban on SIMI, which has been accused of involvement in a number of terror attacks in the country in the last few years.

Jaiswal was at pains to clarify that his letter to Mayawati was not an attempt to prepare the ground for a ban on the Bajrang Dal as well. "This is a matter of internal security. All I have done is to suggest that if the state Government wants, it can request for a CBI probe. Even if the state Government does make the request, it was for CBI to take a final decision on whether this was a fit case for being taken up for investigation," he said.

"I am not asking for a ban on any organisation," he said.

Heading: Valley still under curfew, toll up to six - Indian Express
Content:
As India and the US work overtime to get a clean NSG waiver, the Bush Administration has said the Indo-US atomic deal was currently the "principal focus" of its nuclear policy and given a priority over a similar pact with Russia.

Asked whether developments in Georgia will affect the US-Russia civilian nuclear deal, US Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice said the present focus of America's nuclear commerce policy was the India deal and not the one with Russia.

"Our principal focus right now has been on the India civil nuclear deal, having worked through the IAEA, now working through the NSG, and still trying to get into a position to make the appropriate presidential determinations in early September. So that's our focus right now on the civil nuclear side," Rice told reporters on her way to Tel Aviv.

Rice's comments came even as Foreign Secretary Shiv Shankar Menon discussed a strategy with senior US officials in Washington to address reservations expressed by some countries at the Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) over the draft waiver that is required to push the Indo-US nuke deal forward.

Echoing Rice's sentiments, White House Deputy Press Secretary Tony

Fratto said the current focus of the administration was to see the India-US deal through.

Heading: Communal clashes in Poonch, Mandi - Indian Express
Content:
A civilian, wounded at Hajin when the CRPF and the J-K Police opened fire on the protestors on Tuesday, succumbed to injuries on Wednesday, taking the death toll in the Valley since Sunday to six. Meanwhile, as the entire Kashmir valley continued to be under strict curfew for the third consecutive day, the police arrested three more separatist leaders.

The people in Srinagar city and other major towns of Kashmir faced a shortage of essential items as food stocks began to run out. In the evening, when a milk van reached Magarmal Bagh in civil lines city, people rushed out of their homes to fetch milk for the first time in three days. CRPF personnel posted nearby allegedly went on a rampage and beat up the people. They reportedly fired in the air and also broke window panes of more than 30 houses and pelted stones. "When we told them that we are buying milk here, they turned violent," said Mudasir Ahmad, a resident of Magarmal Bagh.

Defying the curfew, people took to the streets at Bemina in Srinagar, Achabal and Dooru in south Kashmir. At Dooru and Achabal, the CRPF dispersed the protestors with a baton charge. The villagers, however, accused the CRPF personnel of ransacking their houses and beating them up.

People from Pulwama and several other parts of the Valley, where the Army has been deployed, also reported similar stories.

This is the strictest curfew in Kashmir in the past 20 years; it is difficult for even doctors and people with curfew passes to move around Srinagar and other major towns of the Valley. At Regal Chowk in Srinagar, two mediapersons were beaten up by the CRPF when they were on their way to perform professional duties. Doctors at Sheri Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences (SKIMS) said two people who were wounded on Monday managed to reach hospital only on Tuesday because of the curfew.

Heading: Cong leaders meet Sonia - Indian Express
Content:
Fresh communal tensions flared up in Poonch and Mandi towns late on Monday night and Tuesday when they clashed with each other.

Defying the curfew, Muslims took out three separate processions and moved towards the main town at around 11:30 pm. After reaching there, the mob of over a thousand people also raised provocative slogans. Soon, people from the Hindu community came out of their houses and countered the slogans. This led to stone pelting from both sides, which continued till security forces reached the spot around 12.30 am and dispersed the mob. One Vijay Kumar has been arrested in connection with the rioting.

A similar incident was also witnessed at Allah Peer Mohalla and Mandi town where Hindus took out protest rallies and demanded a judicial inquiry and compensation for shops and vehicles allegedly burnt by Muslims in four areas of the district on August 22.

Though curfew was in force in Poonch town, a protest rally was again organised on the day at Mandi. DIG of Rajouri-Poonch, Prithvi Raj Manhas said the situation was under control in all the areas of the district but curfew wasn't relaxed in Poonch town. Meanwhile, members of both communities held a joint meeting in some parts of the district and formed a committee named "Aman Shanti".

Heading: Ansari moves SC over stay of trial in MLA murder case - Indian Express
Content: A delegation of Congress leaders and MPs from Jammu on Tuesday called on Congress President Sonia Gandhi and AICC General Secretary in charge of Jammu & Kashmir Prithviraj Chavan separately to seek immediate action from the Centre to end the crisis over the Amarnath land row in the state. Earlier in the day, the Congress president had a meeting with External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee and Defence Minister AK Antony to discuss the situation in Jammu and the Kashmir Valley. The leaders from Jammu were learnt to be in favour of an across-the-table discussion with leaders from Kashmir to resolve the crisis.

Heading: Godhra riots panel gets more time - Indian Express
Content:
Uttar Pradesh Independent MLA Mukhtar Ansari, the key accused in BJP legislator Krishnanand Rai murder case, on Tuesday moved the Supreme Court alleging that the CBI secured a stay on the proceedings of the case in Ghazipur trial court in a surreptitious manner. The Supreme Court will hear the matter on September 1.

Senior advocate Sushil Kumar, appearing for Ansari, alleged that the CBI secured stay on the case proceedings in the trial court without informing the accused about filing of its petition.

"I (Ansari) am not a party. Please make me a party in the petition. None of the accused is a party in it," Kumar said while referring to the CBI's petition on which the apex court on August 1 had passed its order.

The investigating agency, however, opposed his allegation and said it would file a counter application.

"Mukhtar Ansari is applicant and I have to say a lot," Solicitor General G E Vahanvati submitted before a Bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan, which then posted the matter for hearing on September 1.

The CBI had challenged the Allahabad High Court order, permitting the Ghazipur court to hear bail matters relating to the case.

Besides Ansari, his brother Afzal Ansari (Samajwadi Party MP) and four othergangsters are facing trial in the case.

While challenging the HC order, Vahanvati had contended that the Ghazipur court cannot conduct any criminal proceedings in the case, as the apex court had in August last year restrained it from proceeding with the trial since an application seeking shifting of the case to Lucknow was pending with it. The High Court had not agreed with the CBI contention.

The Solicitor General on August 1 had submitted that the trial be transferred to Lucknow, as relatives of the victim were worried that witnesses would not depose out of fear.

Heading: Judge’s appointment: full-time hearing in HC - Indian Express
Content:
Following the submission of the preliminary report by the five member Special Investigation Team (SIT) reinvestigating the post-Godhra communal riots, the Supreme Court on Tuesday gave an extention till December 31 to the committee to turn in its final report. Senior Advocate Harish Salve, who in his capacity as amicus curiae submitted the report to the court, had sought more time for the SIT to complete its investigations.

The three judge bench comprising Justices Arijit Pasayat, P Sathasivam and Aftab Alam put on record their appreciation of the work done by the SIT while granting the extension."They are doing a good job. Let us give them some more time," observed the bench.

The SIT was constituted by the Apex Court on March 25 this year in response to a 2003 NHRC petition for transfer of the case and trial outside Gujarat due to the threats faced by the witnesses, most of whom had turned hostile.

Heading: Top Naxal leaders surrender - Indian Express
Content:
The hearing has begun in the case pertaining to the appointment of a Allahabad High Court judge after an objection by Additional Solicitor General of India Ashok Nigam against the petition challenging the appointment was rejected on Monday by a Division Bench comprising Justices Shushil Harkauli and Vikram Nath. The petition by advocate M C Gupta alleged that the appointment of Justice Satish Chandra was unconstitutional. Nigam had submitted that Gupta had no locus standi in the case.

On Tuesday, the Bench decided to hold full-time hearing. Till now, the petition was being heard for only two hours in the post-lunch session.

The petition says the information on the official HC website about Satish Chandra were scanty, as compared to the information available on other judges. Only one relevant fact revealed on the website regarding Satish Chandra was that he had worked as a judicial member of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal. It also says his career profile is full of gaps and loose ends. For instance, it does not mention as to from where he obtained his LLB, LLM or LD degrees. It also does not throw any light on his career as an advocate.

In his petition, Gupta alleged that Satish Chandra had neither put in 10 years of practice as a High Court advocate nor had he held a judicial office under the High Court, as per the norms of the Constitution.

Heading: Ministry identifies crops to lure away growers from tobacco - Indian Express
Content:
A divisional committee member of the CPI (Maoist), Suresh Harami, surrendered before the Gadchiroli police along with a dalam commander, a deputy dalam commander and two dalam members on Tuesday.

Suresh alias Jairam Harami, 42, joined the Naxal movement in the early '90s. Additional Director General of Police Pankaj Gupta pointed out that the surrender of such high-ranking Naxalites is a very significant developement. The surrendered cadres have reportedly told the police that they were tired of injustice by their higher-ups, who were imposing on them cadres from outside the state.

"We will present their case for surrender benefits before the District Collector's panel after due verification of further details," said Gupta. He added that the surrendered cadres spoke of widespread resentment amongst local cadres against "unfair treatment". "We are expecting more surrenders in future," he said. With these, 298 Naxal cadres have so far surrendered in Gadchiroli (287) and Gondia (11) districts. Of these, three are dalam commanders.

Heading: China works on matching India’s naval fleet - Indian Express
Content:
As a strong tobacco lobby is trying hard to keep pictorial warnings on their products at bay, the Union Health Ministry along with the Central Tobacco Research Institute (CTRI) and the Union Agriculture Ministry has short-listed a few crops that can be viable alternatives for tobacco growers. The Health Ministry has been trying to introduce pictorial warnings for more than a year now. The tobacco lobby so far has refused to relent, saying it would affect their business and would make them jobless.

Now, the ministry has identified soyabean, gram crop, turmeric and chilli as alternative crops that could be as profitable as growing tobacco. They can also be grown on the same soil.

"The framework convention of tobacco control says to work on strategies to reduce its supply is to control illicit trade and provide alternative employment. The research and various studies done by the CTRI have proved that these crops are as advantageous as tobacco," said a senior official in the ministry.

The ministry, however, believes that the transformation would take time, as it is not easy to change the mindset of the people involved in the trade. "Those involved in growing tobacco believe there will be a negative pattern financially if they start growing other crops," added the official.

According to official data, 1,50,000 tonnes of tobacco and 30,000 tonnes of tendu leaves are used in the manufacture of bidis. The Food and Agriculture Ministry estimates that there are 2.9 lakh tobacco growers in India, engaging about 44 lakh bidi workers in the fields, in the year 1997.

"Tobacco in all its forms is harmful and particularly a big contributor to non-communicable diseases. Anti-tobacco advocacy is the major task of the ministry and that's why we have flagged off the issue and have identified alternative crops," the official said.

According to estimates, 85 per cent of the world's bidi tobacco is grown in India, occupying about 35 per cent of the total area under tobacco cultivation, and concentrated mostly in Gujarat, Karnataka and Maharashtra. The Health Ministry says that cheap labour and better workmanship make West Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka the major centres of bidi rolling. "The state governments will have to be informed about the new research, as the ministry's aim is to reduce tobacco usage which will go down only if the production goes down," the official said.

HOLY SMOKE

•In India, 19% of tobacco consumption is in the form of cigarettes.

• 53% is consumed in the form of bidis.

• The rest is mainly smokeless form

Heading: Jaya aide’s relatives sentenced in DA case - Indian Express
Content:
China is set to get its first functional aircraft carrier -- a refurbished Soviet-era Kiev class warship -- by 2012 and will use it exclusively to train Navy personnel for the three indigenous carriers it plans to induct over the next decade.

While it is a known fact that the defunct Varyag aircraft carrier that was purchased from Ukraine as scrap for $20 million in 1998 was planned as a training platform for the Chinese Navy, India now believes that the warship will be ready for basic training operations as early as 2012.

The ship has been renamed as the Shilang and has been transferred to the Dalian Naval Academy for induction as a training platform, latest intelligence inputs available with strategic think tanks suggest.

The carrier, which was left two-thirds complete by the USSR and lacked a propulsion system when it was sold as scrap to a Macau-based company, is being fitted with a Chinese power plant and will sail out of the Dalian dock by 2012 -- the year India is expecting the Gorshkov carrier to arrive from Russia -- and will be used to carry out basic landing and take off practice.

While the 67,000-ton carrier will not be able to carry out full fledged maritime operations, it will be fully ready for training purposes by 2012 to pave the way for the induction of three aircraft carriers that China is manufacturing indigenously.

Analysts say that though India is currently ahead in the maritime domain and has been operating aircraft carriers since 1961 when it commissioned the British origin INS Vikrant, China is fast catching up with its nuclear submarine programme and the intention to acquire an aircraft carrier fleet.

However, it could take the country up to two decades -- the time required to train crews and fine-tune operations aboard warships of this size -- to have a fully operational aircraft carrier group, analysts say.

While the Chinese project has been kept under wraps, India has already publicly announced its indigenous aircraft carrier programme. Work on the first Air Defence Ship (ADS) has already started at the Cochin Shipyard and the order for a second indigenous carrier is likely to be placed by next year.

India's sole carrier, the INS Viraat, is set for decommissioning by 2012 by which time the Gorshkov is expected to arrive.

Navy Chief Admiral Sureesh Mehta has expressed his concern about the increasing number of nuclear submarines in India's neighbourhood in reference to China's new generation nuclear submarines that have come to light over the past year.

Heading: Student held for forging papers posing as govt official - Indian Express
Content:
S R Bhaskaran and his wife Sreelatha Devi, relatives of AIADMK supremo J Jayalalithaa's aide Sasikala, were sentenced in a disproportionate assets case by a special CBI court on Tuesday. While Bhaskaran, a former Reserve Bank of India employee, was awarded five years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs 20 lakh, his wife Sreelatha, Sasikala's sister-in-law, was handed down a three-year jail term and a Rs 10 lakh fine for amassing wealth in excess of known sources of income.

Bhaskaran, Sreelatha and her brother TTV Dinakaran, Rajya Sabha member and husband of Sasikala, were chargesheeted in 1998 for accumulating wealth to the tune of Rs 2 crore. Though Bhaskaran argued that the wealth was part of a family fortune inherited by him, the judge ruled it was clearly over and above his known sources of income. Sreelatha also played a role in the dealings, Judge Naganathan had said.

Bhaskaran's name had earlier cropped up in the colour TV distribution case in which Jayalalithaa, Sasikala and former AIADMK minister T M Selvaganapathi were the main accused, with everyone but Selvaganapathi being acquitted. An appeal by the Government is pending at the Madras High Court in this regard.

Heading: Abhaya case: CBI says it got just one narco-analysis test CD - Indian Express
Content:
The Chhattisgarh Police are examining a laptop and cellphone records of an engineering student who was arrested with a fake identify card, purported to have been issued by Rashtrapati Bhavan, after he posed as chairman of a "'High-Powered Committee of Anti-Naxal Squad".

Rohit Vajpayee, who claimed to be chairman of an "Anti-Naxal Squad", fell into the police net after he had a spat with the traffic police during a routine security check before the movement of the convoy of state Governor E S L Narasimhan. Police seized his car fitted with a red beacon light and a board indicating "chairman, High Powered Committee of Anti-Naxal Squad".

In order to influence the police, Rohit flashed an identify card, having an Ashoka emblem and supposed to have been issued by the President's secretariat, and other documents regarding his appointment to the post. He also claimed that the committee was constituted during the tenure of Dr A P J Abdul Kalam as President.

Suspecting foul play, police got in touch with the President's secretariat, which confirmed that all documents, including the identity card, were fake and no such committee existed. Subsequently, Rohit was arrested and produced before a court, which remanded him to police custody till August 31 for questioning.

Additional Superintendent of Police Ajajshatru Bahadur Singh said a laptop, seized from his possession, has been sent for detailed examination as it contained scanned copies of a number of specimen signatures, which were apparently being used to forge documents. Call details of his cellphone were also being verified to ascertain his activities and links, he added.

Investigations could not progress as Rohit complained of uneasiness and was hospitalised. Police are trying to find out whether he is involved in criminal activities.

Heading: BSF to maintain pillars on Indo-Bangla border - Indian Express
Content:
The CBI which is investigating the murder of Catholic nun Abhaya informed the Kerala High Court on Tuesday that it had received only a single CD of the narco-analysis tests conducted on three primary suspects in the case.

Earlier, the court had asked the Central Forensic Lab in Bangalore to directly produce the CD of the narco tests, after the court developed suspicion that the content of the tests had been tampered with. Accordingly, the CFL produced three CDs of the tests done on Fr Thomas Pithrikkayail, Fr Jose Kottoor and Sr Stefy. The lab, in a letter to the court, said three CDs had been send to CBI hadquarters in New Delhi.

However, CBI DySP R K Agarwal presented the letter from the lab addressed to the CBI, which had reference to only one CD. Hence, the agency reiterated that it had obtained only a single CD. The CBI produced the letter in the court when the judge remarked that the investigating agency was making a false statement on the number of CDs of the tests. Judge V Ramkumar has sought the CD of the test, while hearing an appeal of Abhaya's father Thomas Aikkarakkunnel, seeking a direction to the CBI to speed up the probe.

Heading: IIM boards should decide on fee hike: review panel - Indian Express
Content:
With a number of instances of shifting of boundary pillars on the Indo-Bangladesh border coming to the notice of the Government, the task of maintaining these pillars has been taken away from state governments and entrusted to the Border Security Force (BSF).

Till now, the boundary pillars were maintained by the governments of West Bengal, Tripura or Assam in their respective regions but recently there have been reports of a number of these pillars either being shifted or completely demolished by miscreants. This can have serious implications in terms of alteration of the international border.

Accordingly, the Ministry of External Affairs, which funds the maintenance of these pillars, suggested that the job be entrusted to the BSF which already looks after the boundary pillars on the Pakistan border.

The BSF informed their Bangladesh counterparts, the Bangladesh Rifles (BDR), about this development at the DG level meeting last week, BSF DG A K Mitra told reporters on Monday. The two forces have worked out an arrangement by which the BSF will look after the even numbers of pillars while the BDR will maintain the odd numbers, Mitra said.

Briefing the reporters about the meeting, Mitra said the two forces had agreed to make an assessment to identify sensitive areas on the about 4,000-km border which can then be put under joint patrol. The Indian side has already made such an assessment and given a copy to the BDR, he said.

The two sides had also agreed to resolve the border development projects which have been pending because of objections by either of the forces. He said 18 such projects would be resolved by the end of this month itself.

The BSF DG provided the Bangladeshi side a list of 213 people, who are wanted for various crimes within India and are reported to have taken shelter in Bangladesh. The BDR was also handed a list of 110 terrorist camps, which India believes, are used for training and housing terrorists who plan and carry out terror attacks in the country.

Heading: RAW says no proof to back Bhatia charges - Indian Express
Content:
As the meetings between the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) review committee and the Human Resource Development (HRD) Ministry take place, a view is developing that though autonomy of the elite institute should not be challenged, it should also be conveyed that the fee hike is exactly not desirable.

The three-member review committee, which held a meeting with the HRD Ministry on Tuesday, is also likely to recommend a huge increase in the number of seats at IIMs — almost three-fold —according to official sources.

The committee, formed to review the functioning of all the IIMs in the country, has already submitted an interim report to the Ministry and a final report is expected in a month's time. The IIMs had introduced fee hikes this year, with IIM-Ahmedabad quoting the highest percentage. The Ministry feels the hikes come in the way of an equitable and accessible education system. "We will submit our recommendations to the government next month," head of the committee and Maruti Udyog CEO R C Bhargava said after the meeting.

It has been learnt that the committee report will advocate a middle path on the fee hike issue.

Heading: Will review proposed quota for IIT faculty, assures PM - Indian Express
Content:
The Nisha Bhatia case is the first serious complaint taken up by the Sexual Harassment Committee (SHC) set up years ago by the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW), as per the guidelines issued by Supreme Court. And ironically enough, in 2004, Bhatia was the one picked by the agency to be the chairperson of the SHC, an offer she declined since she was posted at the agency's high-security training institute in Gurgaon.

The Indian Express has accessed the 87-page confidential inquiry report on allegations made by Bhatia, submitted to RAW chief Ashok Chaturvedi on May 19.

Its contents reveal that Bhatia's complaints of sexual harassment by joint secretary Sunil Uke was the only item on the committee's agenda and allegations she made against Chaturvedi himself were not part of the inquiry.

Interestingly, both Bhatia and Uke say they have till date not been given a copy of the report. The SHC concluded that it could find "no proof" to substantiate Bhatia's complaints against Uke, but said the officer exhibited a "discriminatory attitude towards a junior female colleague, which itself violates the spirit of right to gender equality, as laid down by SC guidelines on the issue".

The SHC was headed by RAW joint secretary Shashi Prabha and had a co-opted member, National Security Council director Tara Kantha. It also noted that "Ms Bhatia's threats to take her own life, as well as the threats (faced by her) from other quarters, appear to indicate a disturbed state of mind. As such, counselling may benefit her".

The report also points out that "Nisha Bhatia's repeated refusal to appear before the committee despite as many as seven notices being sent to her constrained the committee from making any meaningful assessment of these issues". Besides Bhatia's complaints, the report contains written statements of Sunil Uke, copies of SMSes sent by the complainant to members of RAW and the SHC, as well as the testimonies of junior officials in the agency who worked with the two officers.

The SHC also made these recommendations in its report:

•The department may draw the attention of lady officers that genuine instances of sexual exploitation/harassment may be filed with the committee with some material evidence to substantiate the charges. They must also be prepared to cooperate with the committee if they lodge a complaint.

•It is suggested as a confidence-building measure, the committee may meet quarterly to review/assess the position obtaining in the department (RAW) with reference to sexual harassment cases and implementation of preventive steps outlined in SC guidelines on the subject.

While Bhatia did not appear before the SHC, Uke deposed twice and said he "denies all allegations and charges" and alleged that the complainant was "mentally sick and has bouts of frenzied behaviour".

Who is Sunil Uke

Sunil Uke, an officer of the Indian Revenue Service, served on deputation with the RAW for nine years and was also given plum foreign postings by the agency. In September 2007, he reverted to his cadre and is presently posted as a Customs Commissioner in Haryana.

When contacted, he only said, "I had nothing personal against Nisha Bhatia and wish her well. But I would like to advise her to take medical treatment, which as I told the committee in New Delhi, I think she badly needs."

Heading: Centre to Meghalaya: start uranium mining, get Rs 800 cr for development - Indian Express
Content:
Prime Minister Manmohan Singh would take up the issue of exempting recruitment of faculty in the Indian Institutes of technology (IIT) from the government's reservation policy.

Singh said this in response to a request made by Prof Gautam Baruah, director, IIT Guwahati, while he was welcoming the PM to the inauguration of a TCS Learning Centre there. Baruah said, "I would like to make a request, not only for this IIT, but on behalf of all the IITs. This is to do with reservations in faculty recruitment."

Baruah said that since 1972, through a Government order, exemption from reservation has been granted in recruiting scientists and researchers in nationally important institutes of the departments of Space, Atomic Energy and Defence. "The IITs also have not had reservation for faculty since then. It has recently been said the exemption for IITs is only de facto," he said.

"Introducing reservation in faculty recruitment at IITs after 36 years will create problems. Especially now, as shortage of faculty is likely to become more acute with the establishment of 8 new IITs."

Responding to this appeal, Singh said he would surely place the matter in the Cabinet. "I take note of the point that Prof. Gautam Baruah has made with regard to the reservation issue. I will bring it to the notice of my Cabinet colleagues," the PM said.

Singh also said that the UPA Government had embarked on a huge knowledge investment in the 11th Plan Period to the tune of Rs 2,75, 000 crore. The aim is to create a pool of 500 million trained human resources by 2020 by undertaking an 'education revolution', he added

Heading: 5 more seats for tribals in Meghalaya med college - Indian Express
Content:
The sanction of Rs 800 crore by the Centre for infrastructure development in uranium-rich West Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya has come with a rider.

With the Uranium Corporation of India Limited (UCIL) gearing to take up mining in the Kylleng-Pyndensohiong-Mawthabah areas of the district, the Meghalaya Government will have to reach a consensus over the mining issue if it wants the Centre to invest there.

Union Cabinet Secretary K M Chandrasekhar held a meeting on Monday with Union Government secretaries, Meghalaya Chief Secretary Ranjan Chatterjee and officials of UCIL and Atomic Energy Commission (AEC) officials. "The Union Government has sanctioned Rs 800 crore for development of infrastructure provided the Meghalaya Government is able to evolve a consensus over the mining issue," Chatterjee said on Tuesday.

Anti-mining groups like the Khasi Students' Union (KSU) and political parties like Hills State People Democratic Party (HSPDP) and Khun Hynniewtrep National Awakening Movement (KHNAM) have been opposing uranium mining, arguing that radiation caused by it will affect health and environment.

"The meeting felt if development is put on fast track in the area, the apprehension of opposing groups will lessen," said Chatterjee.

Chatterjee said Rs 800 crore has been sanctioned to set up five Public Health Centres, a Community Health Centre, a Kendra Vidhalaya School, a polytechnic institute and water supply connection in the area.

Heading: The bajrang bomb? - Indian Express
Content:
After threatening to discontinue the MBBS course at North Eastern Indira Gandhi Regional Institute of Health and Medical Sciences (NEIGRIHMS) in Meghalaya if the Khasi Students' Union (KSU) continued to pressurise the Union Health Ministry for 30 per cent seat-reservation for tribals, Union Health Secretary Naresh Dayal agreed to grant five more seats to placate the students' body.

NEIGRIHMS has 50 MBBS seats of which 24 seats will be reserved for students from other northeastern states which do not have medical colleges.

In a meeting held in New Delhi on Tuesday, Dayal reportedly told Meghalaya Chief Secretary Ranjan Chatterjee that the Centre was willing to discontinue the MBBS course in NEIGRIHMS if the KSU tried to armtwist the Government into conceding to its demand of 30 per cent seat reservation for tribals.

The KSU had earlier stalled the MBBS entrance examination that was to be held in Shillong on August 3 to pressurise the Ministry into conceding to its demand. The Ministry then decided to hold the entrance examination in Guwahati but the KSU had protested.

NEIGRIHMS then postponed the examination and Chatterjee flew to New Delhi to hold talks with ministry officials. "Five additional seats will be for Meghalaya's tribals, above the nine seats reserved for Meghalaya," Chatterjee told The Indian Express after the meeting. Of the nine seats, two were to be reserved for NEIGRIHMS faculty members' children.

The KSU had objected to reservation for faculty members' children demanding that all nine seats be open to all candidates from Meghalaya. With five additional seats, Meghalaya will now have 14 seats of which two will be reserved for faculty members' children.

Chatterjee said the ministry was willing to review the reservation of seats in the next academic session.

Heading: The Sangh Parivar’s lumpen fringe - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when probes in several recent serial blasts have led investigators to Uttar Pradesh, the explosion in Kanpur on August 24 made everyone take note. However, the findings are not what the police may have bargained for. The two who died in the blast were making explosive devices at the time and, it is believed, had links with a Hindu outfit. What also surprised investigators was the quantity of explosives found.

While the Bajrang Dal has since owned up both Rajeev Mishra and Bhupinder Singh — though adding that they were inactive members of the outfit — the police have said they have no evidence to confirm the same. While Kanpur zone IG S N Singh admits that "the recovery reveals the plan was for a massive explosion", the police have no idea as to where the explosives came from or what these were meant for.

Incidentally, Singh had five cases registered against him in the 1992 riots, including one of arrest with a petrol bomb. Mishra had no known criminal record.

The blast that killed Mishra and Singh took place in a house owned by Mishra's father in Rajeev Nagar. The house functioned as a private hostel for students and the room in which the explosion took place was used by Mishra, who worked in Lucknow and visited Kanpur every Sunday. Manager of the hostel Raj Kishore Srivastava said Singh and Mishra had met each other during the meetings of the Bajrang Dal and become friends.

When the police arrived after the blast on Sunday, it found in the room 3 kg lead oxide, 500 grammes red lead, 1 kg potassium nitrate, 11 countrymade grenades, several bomb pins, seven timers and batteries — all meant for making improvised explosive devices. The countrymade hand grenades, which the police say were hollow, were similar in shape and size to those used by the defence forces.

The provincial general secretary of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad, Awadh Behari Mishra, told The Indian Express: "Both (Mishra and Singh) were members of the Bajrang Dal, but had been inactive for a long time." Though Mishra was just a member of the Bajrang Dal, Singh held the important post of Kanpur City Convener in 2001-02.

"After his marriage, Bhupinder became inclined towards his professional career and did not take much interest in our activities," the VHP leader said. "Similarly, Rajeev too was a Bajrang Dal member but was inactive as he was working in Lucknow and came to Kanpur only once a week." He added that neither Mishra nor Singh was involved in illegal activities.

Bajrang Dal national convenor Prakash Sharma claimed the same. "Rajeev and Bhupinder have maintained a distance from the organisation for long and were not in touch with any of the senior members." He said he had no knowledge of their involvement in any illegal activity.

SSP of Kanpur Ashok Kumar Singh, however, said he is still not convinced the two were Bajrang Dal members. "We do not have any official papers to prove this," he said.

Admitting that they were yet to make a breakthrough, IG Singh said the police were looking into the antecedents of Mishra and Singh, questioning their relatives, and studying their cellphone records. While Mishra's family has come out to say that they have had no relations with their son for a long time, Bhupinder's has shunned the media.

In raids on Singh's Lajpat Nagar photo studio and his residence, the police have found a hand-drawn map of Ferozabad and a diary. Some powder was also found at his residence, though different from the substance found at the blast site. SSP Singh said they had spoken to Vijay who worked as an assistant at Singh's photo studio, but he had not provided any significant leads.

Bhupinder Singh's record shows five cases against his name in the 1992 riots, all registered at the Kakadeo police station. On August 31, 1997, one Virendra Pratap had registered a case with the Kalyanpur police station against Uday Shankar, Om Mishra and Daljit Singh and alleged them of attacking him. Though Singh's name was not included in the FIR, Virendra Pratap had accused him of firing and hurling countrymade bombs during a Trade Committee election at Ram Lalla Vidyalaya, Rawatpur.

Shakya said: "Virendra has claimed that Bhupinder had fired a bullet and hurled countrymade bombs at him." Virendra and one Guddu Mishra were injured in the incident.

Questions have been raised over the fact that the police got a student of the hostel where the blast happened to file an FIR instead of filing one themselves. It was this student, Pradeep Soni, who had called up the police after the explosion. Soni is apprehensive now of being dragged into the case. IG Singh, however, played this down. From a legal point of view, "it is better that a local resident lodges the case", he says.

More explosives found

A stone's throw away from the Kanpur house where explosives were recovered on Sunday, similar seizures were made on Tuesday morning. The two empty shells and explosives were found in a jute bag in a drain in the Shastri Nagar area under the Kalyanpur Police Station after some people noticed it and alerted the police. Kanpur zone IG S N Singh said the shells could carry one kg explosive. The powder that was also recovered would be sent to IIT-Kanpur for tests.

Heading: Nine, to the power of Two - Indian Express
Content:
If the BJP treats the RSS as its ideological mentor, the Bajrang Dal is certainly the Sangh Parivar's lumpen fringe. Largely constituted of unemployed youth of urban India, the Bajrang Dal, otherwise known to exist on the fringes of the Hindutva family, springs to life on occasions like Valentine's Day or in cities with mixed religious demographic profile. Bajrang Dal activists fashion themselves as "vigilantes", protecting what essentially is their notion of "Hindu pride and Hindu nationalism".

The Bajrang Dal started essentially as a loose grouping of the urban youth looking for some identity in the mid 80s. And they found it in the Ayodhya agitation. Present BJP general secretary Vinay Katiyar, then known more as a free-wheeling rabble rouser, was one of the first few to undertake a yatra for a Ram Temple in Ayodhya. He then went on to become the founder-president of the Bajrang Dal.

The organisation, recall old-timers, was not a recognised affiliate of the Sangh Parivar. It was only when the organisation started an agitation for the Ayodhya temple that it was merged with the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), after a resolution to this effect was passed by the latter.

While Katiyar came to be known as the founder-president of the Bajrang Dal, he was followed by Jaibhan Singh Pawaiya (who came into limelight after he, as a BJP nominee, took on Madhavrao Scinida in an epic battle for the Lok Sabha seat from Gwalior in 1999) and Surendra Dada Jain, now a senior functionary in the VHP. Present Bajrang Dal chief Prakash Sharma, incidentally, hails from Kanpur where a blast at a house on Saturday night claimed lives of two men who are believed to be affiliated to the outfit.

The Bajrang Dal, unlike the RSS and the VHP, has not attracted any serious academic work. It is, however, not known to have an organised hierarchy or even an organisation, like, say, in the RSS. Its activities include "agitations for a Ram Temple in Ayodhya; stirs against cow slaughter, religious conversions, and infiltration".

Heading: Adoption racket connects India, Australia - Indian Express
Content:
Even at a time when horsetrading saw bundles of cash land in Parliament, Jharkhand's is a case uniquely its own. In three years since March 2005, the state has seen three governments, and is now preparing for the fourth. While Shibu Soren would point out that he is back at the helm, the true winners of this game of musical chairs have been the Independents. If Madhu Koda set a record as the longest-serving chief minister elected as an Independent, those supporting him haven't done so badly either. Having switched loyalties to Soren, they are likely to stay as ministers. MANOJ PRASAD talks to them ahead of government formation

•MADHU KODA: A graduate from Ranchi University, he began his political career as a member of the RSS before he joined the BJP and won from the Jagannathpur ST (Reserved) constituency in 2000. After Jharkhand was formed, he became Minister (Parliamentary Affairs) in the NDA government led by the BJP's Babulal Marandi. In 2005, denied tickets by the BJP, he contested as an Independent and retained his Jagannathpur seat. In March 2005, he was back as Minister (Mines) in the NDA government led by Arjun Munda. However, barely 17 months later, on September 17, 2006, Koda along with three fellow Independents in the Munda cabinet — Kamlesh Singh, Harinarain Rai and Enos Ekka — toppled the government. The next day, with the Congress, RJD and JMM backing him, he became the Chief Minister.

After the JMM withdrew support to his government earlier this month, Koda, who had retained many portfolios (including the crucial Mines in this mineral-rich state), tendered his resignation declaring that he would never support Soren. The resolve lasted three days. Now among those lined up behind Soren, Koda insists he has no plans to join the new government. However, he adds a rider: "In case any responsibility is given to me, I will not shirk."

•BANDHU TIRKEY: A graduate from Ranchi University, he worked as a bank manager before he quit to join hands with RJD chief Lalu Prasad Yadav. In 2005, he contested the election on a United Goa Democratic Party ticket and won from the ST (Reserved) Mandar constituency. During the Munda government, he sat on the opposition benches. Having played a key role in toppling Munda, he was rewarded by Koda with the portfolio of Minister (Human Resources).

Earlier this month, as Soren made it clear that he wanted the Jharkhand chief ministership, Tirkey switched sides to the JMM. Ask him if he is among the various admirers of 'Guruji' (as Soren is called), and Tirkey only says: "Any portfolio will be acceptable to me."

•JOBA MANJHI: Her husband Devendra Manjhi began his political innings as a JMM worker and represented the Manoharpur ST (Reserved) constituency twice, in 1980 and 1985. After he was shot dead, she contested the seat as an Independent in 2000 and won. Marandi made her a minister in his government. Even after Marandi was replaced by Munda, Manjhi stayed as minister. When Munda too was toppled, she slipped to the Koda camp.

Now, since Wednesday, her loyalties lie with Soren. Though elections are a mere one and a half years away, Manjhi has high hopes of Soren: "In this short time, I would like this government to work for creating employment opportunities for people."

•ENOS EKKA: He was a contractor with the Indian Railways when he entered the political arena. He won the Kolebira ST (Reserved) seat in 2005, and joined the Munda cabinet as Minister (Rural Development). As Munda's ship sank, Ekka deserted him for Koda and managed to retain the portfolio.

All indications showing that he would figure in the Soren ministry, Ekka is clear on his priorities. Plagued by allegations of corruption, he says: "Speedier development is the need of the hour."

•STEPHEN MARANDI: Beginning his career as a JMM leader, he fell out with Soren over the latter's attempt to prop up wife Rupi as party president. Marandi quit the JMM to contest the Dumka ST (Reserved) seat as an Independent in 2005. He found himself in power after he helped Koda topple Munda. While he reportedly demanded the Energy portfolio, he was placated with a deputy chief ministership, with Finance.

Along with Koda, he was among the last ones to hold out on supporting Soren. His change of heart may have something to do with the promise of returning as deputy CM. If he is denied the post? "We will see," says Marandi.

•HARINARAIN RAI: An unemployed graduate, he found himself in luck when he won as an Independent from the Jarmundi seat in 2005 and became a minister in the Munda cabinet. Later, Koda not only took him in but also gave him the same portfolio of Urban Development. Critics sniggered that while the urban areas of Jharkhand showed no "development", Rai himself had made substantial progress, with houses in Ranchi and Deoghar apart from a dairy farm.

Now with Soren, he hopes to retain the post of Minister (Urban Development). His motivation for the switch was simple, he says. "To avoid President's rule, I have sided with Guruji."

•KAMLESH SINGH: The son of a subordinate court judge, he dealt with building materials and sold bricks before joining politics. In 2005, he won for the first time from Hussinabad on a Nationalist Congress Party ticket. Defying the party, he joined the Munda government as minister, and later, switched over to the Koda camp.

Even before Koda withdrew support, Singh was singing Soren tune. He is confident that Soren will last out his term. "There is no problem. We are there with him," he says.

•BHANU PRATAP SHAHI: The son of socialist leader Hemendra Pratap Shahi, he won for the first time in 2005 from Bahvnathpur as a candidate of the Forward Bloc. After Munda was toppled and Koda came to power, he backed it defying the party directive. While he himself was in jail on charges of assaulting government staff in two cases, Koda rewarded his father with a ministerial post. Once out on bail, Shahi replaced father as Minister (Health).

Wooed over by Soren, Shahi says: "Nobody wants mid-term polls. Had we not backed him, President's rule was inevitable."

•APARNA SEN GUPTA: After her husband, a Forward Bloc MLA from Nirsa constituency, was shot, she contested the seat on a party ticket and won it in 2005. Unlike Shahi, she stayed in the opposition both during the Munda and Koda regimes.

In search of allies, Soren contacted her. Asked what prompted her to do back him, she says it was to prevent President's Rule.

Heading: Parivar rift over VHP leader’s death - Indian Express
Content:
A tamil nadu racket under which children were abducted and then sold for adoption is back in the news three years after it surfaced. After a story in Time magazine about how some of these abducted children may be in Australia, authorities from here to Queensland are conducting a probe. A CBI investigation in 2005 had found that many of the children adopted by foreign couples from the state were kidnapped and sold to them. Touts would abduct the children and hand them over to adoption agencies for anywhere between Rs 500 and 10,000. One such agency, Malaysian Social Service (MSS) in Chennai, was believed to have sent 120 children for adoption to foreign countries, including 13 to Australia alone.

Though government guidelines mandate a preference for in-country adoptions, the focus was always on foster parents from abroad who "donated" money to these agencies.

Interest has peaked in the case again since the Time report and Australian media stories on Julia and Barry Rollings of Canberry, the parents of eight children, who adopted a five-year-old boy and a three-year-old girl from Chennai in 1998. After they heard of the racket, the Rollings conducted a personal investigation of their own into the children's background and traced the biological mother of one of them. Last year, they visited the family.

Sympathising with parents who may still be waiting for their children, Julia has asked for a thorough investigation into the case. "We want an investigation so our children can know for certain what happened. And most importantly so their other mother can get justice. She is the one who has lost the most in all of this," she was quoted as saying in the Australian media. Julia told The Indian Express that they were planning to pay another visit to India soon.

The CBI has now sent letters to interview the authorities and the foster parents in Queensland, while the Federal Government of Queensland has also announced a probe of its own.

However, authorities here and in Australia acknowledge that bringing any of the children back won't be easy. Queensland Premier Anna Bligh refuses to speculate on what will happen to the children. "I think it's far too early to be speculating about that and I think it would be wrong of me given the very complex human issues at heart," she said.

Heading: SIMI held three terror camps in Kota, say police - Indian Express
Content:
At least two BJP ministers in the Naveen Patnaik Government may be forced to resign to mollify the angry cadres of the Sangh Parivar after the killings at Kandhamal last Saturday laid bare the deep divide between the BJP and other saffron outfits like the Vishwa Hindu Parishad and the Bajrang Dal in Orissa.

The split came to the fore on Monday when some legislators of the saffron party blamed the administration for the killings and said they wouldn't allow the Assembly to function until the culprits were arrested. But after Rural Development Minister Biswabhushan Harichandan and Revenue Minister Manmohan Samal, both senior BJP leaders, refused to criticise Patnaik over the murder of Swami Lakshmanananda Saraswati and other VHP men, some MLAs refused to attend the BJP legislature party meeting organised at Biswabhushan's residence. The 13 tribal MLAs among the 33 BJP legislators in the state say they will settle for nothing less than the resignations of the two ministers.

At a Sangh Parivar meeting on Tuesday, the two ministers were asked to put in their papers for failing to criticise the Government. "We have given them an ultimatum to resign from the ministry on their own or else they will be thrown out of the party," said a VHP leader. "I expect the BJP minister to resign after the killings, as the Government has failed to provide security to a renowned leader," said Subash Chouhan, national co-convenor of the Bajrang Dal.

Chouhan is particularly miffed over the Government's claim that Maoists could be behind the killing of the Swami. "The claim is laughable. The Government is trying to cover up its failure. Our ministers could not manage to transfer the Kandhmal SP after he refused to listen to us about the threat to Swami's life," he said.

Emotions are running high in the Sangh after the murder of the seer. Senior leaders are desperately trying to regain their eroding base. "So anyone not seen showing enough vigour in criticising the Government's failure in the case will land in trouble," said an RSS pracharak. Incidentally, Higher Education Minister Sameer Dey has already come out openly against the Government.

VHP international secretary general Praveen Togadia has already set the tone by calling the Patnaik Government an "eunuch administration" while demanding a public apology from the Chief Minister who is caught between the rising Left wing extremism and the spiralling communal violence in Kandhamal. "Naveen and the state police are responsible for this attack orchestrated by the Church," alleged Togadia.

Chouhan said when Australian missionary Graham Staines was killed, it caused an international outrage. But this time even those who owed their political careers to the VHP did not react strongly.

Ashok Sahu, chief of the Hindu Jagaran Samukhya, a RSS frontal organisation, said, "If the BJP ministers have any shame they should resign from their posts and withdraw support to the Government." Rejecting the judicial probe ordered by the Government, he said: "The Government has lost its moral right to govern. We want a CBI probe."

Though the RSS has not come out openly against its ministers, sources said it was tacitly supporting the disgruntled elements who wanted the ministers out.

Since the BJP needs the Biju Janata Dal's support in the coming Lok Sabha polls, it seems improbable the party will pull the rug from under the Government. However, some top BJP leaders and the RSS brass are not averse to the two ministers being sacked to pacify the tribal MLAs and, most importantly, the VHP and Bajrang Dal. The Sangh has always been suspicious of Biswabhushan's leanings, as he has often acted like an acolyte of Patnaik rather than the BJP.

Meanwhile, the Congress on Tuesday served a notice of no-confidence against the Patnaik Government over the killing of the VHP leader.

Heading: Varanasi blasts accused Waliullah gets 10 years in jail - Indian Express
Content:
Even as Shahbaz Hussain, one of the suspected masterminds behind the Jaipur terror strikes on May 13, was remanded to police custody for 10 days, the Rajasthan Police arrested seven more persons from Kota district on Monday night. The police also believe that Hussain along with other suspected SIMI activists, Mufti Abu Bashir and Sajid Mansuri, held as many as three terror camps in Nanta in Kota district between November 2007 and January 2008. They added that the SIMI network suspected of carrying out terror strikes across the country had links with other terror outfits.

Rajasthan Director General of Police (DGP) K S Bains on Tuesday said, "We have found that SIMI activists were trained in Kota, where a large SIMI network has been exposed, before carrying out the May 13 blasts. More information will be available only after questioning Hussain at length." However, a police official, on condition of anonymity, said, "The camps were similar to the one held in Pavagadh near Vadodara before the Ahmedabad blasts. Activists here were trained in arms and were indoctrinated." He added that Hussain and Mansuri visited Kota several times in 2008 and conducted a recce in Jaipur.

In the first breakthrough in the blasts probe, Hussain was arrested on Monday and brought to Jaipur from Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh late on the same night on transit remand. A Rajasthan court on Tuesday remanded him to 10 days in police custody.

Rajasthan ADG (crime) A K Jain, who heads the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the blasts said, "Sajid Mansuri accused in the Ahmedabad terror strikes led us to Hussain. We have also arrested seven others from Kota on Monday who knew Mansuri and could have been involved in the terror strike." Those arrested include Dr Ishaque Qureshi, his son Taufique, who was in Jaipur with Mansuri for two days before the blasts, and Munawar Khan, a tailor. All three are residents of Kota.

DGP Bains said the Jaipur terror strikes were conducted in a complex manner. "We believe the planning was done in one city, the bombs made in another. The terror network's presence has been seen in Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan," Bains said.

Since different modules were involved in carrying out the attacks, it further complicated the investigation, he said, adding, "We are on the lookout for such terror networks in other parts of the state." He also said the SIMI network could possibly have been involved with terror outfits like Lashkar-e-Toiba.

Heading: Trial in 7/11, other MCOCA cases stayed again - Indian Express
Content:
A lucknow court sentenced HuJI member Waliullah to 10 years' imprisonment, finding him guilty of offences under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, on Tuesday. He was also sentenced to three years' imprisonment under the Arms Act.

In his judgment, Additional District Judge S C Tripathi imposed penalties of Rs 1 lakh and Rs 5,000 respectively, under the two Acts, said prosecutor Aslam Siddiqui. "The trial for the offences under the Explosive Act was still pending, as the police are yet to file a chargesheet. Eight witnesses in favour of the prosecution and one from the defence had appeared before the court against Waliullah," he added.

Waliullah, the main accused in the 2006 Varanasi blasts case, was arrested on April 5, 2006 from Lucknow's Gosainganj area. The police had recovered detonators, RDX and a .32-bore pistol from his possession. The trial is still on in a Ghaziabad court.

A case under sections 121-A (conspiracy to commit offences related to waging war against GoI), 122 (collecting arms etc to wage war against GoI), 124-A (sedition), 153-A (doing acts prejudicial to maintenance of harmony), 213 (attempt to conceal offence) and 120-B (hatching conspiracy) of the IPC and Unlawful Activities Act, Explosives Act and Arms Act were registered against him.

Heading: Infiltration in Jammu again - Indian Express
Content:
Six months after it stayed trials in three cases filed under MCOCA, including the 7/11 Mumbai serial blasts case, the Supreme Court on Tuesday extended the interim stay and adjourned the matter till October, when the court hoped a judgment in a "similar case" would be pronounced.

Extending the interim stay ordered on February 29, the Bench comprising Justices L S Panta and R V Raveendran, suggested that the counsel wait for a decision in the said case. "It might have a bearing on the cases (in question)," said Justice Raveendran to Shakil Ahmed Syed, advocate for Zameer Ahmed Latifur Rehman, who had challenged the constitutional validity of certain provisions in the Maharasthra terror law. The matter will be heard on October 14.

On February 29, the Bench headed by Justice B N Agarwal had ordered an interim stay on the trial in the Mumbai serial blasts case, till further orders. Besides the 7/11 case, it had also halted proceedings in the Special MCOCA court pertaining to four bomb explosions that took place on September 8, 2006 at Malegaon. The trial in another case relating to seizure of arms in Aurangabad on May 9, 2006, was also stayed.

Heading: Entries open for India Press Photo Awards 2008 - Indian Express
Content:
A group of militants allegedly crossed over into India early on Tuesday after cutting the barbed wire along the international border in Kanachak sector of Jammu.

In New Delhi, Defence Minister A K Antony said though the increasing number of cross-border firings were a cause for concern, the ceasefire agreement with Pakistan should remain in place. "This year, the cross-border firing incidents are more. But that does not mean the entire border is troublesome. Even now I feel we have to hold on to the ceasefire agreement," Antony said, adding that very few militants have managed to sneak in due to the Army's efforts.

Kanachak was the second major infiltration since May, when a group of militants managed to sneak into Indian territory under cover of heavy fire from the Pakistani side in Samba sector and gunned down five people.

Sources said the militants used the same modus operandi this time too. A group of over 20 militants took positions close to the border around 12.45 am and opened fire on BSF pickets. The BSF personnel retaliated and the exchange of fire between the two sides continued for nearly an hour. However, taking advantage of the exchange of fire, some militants cut the barbed wire fence near the Laliyal border outpost and sneaked into Indian territory.

BSF's Deputy Inspector General G S Virk confirmed that three to four militants were seen moving towards India. "We fired at them, but they managed to escape," he said. He added that the BSF seized nearly nine magazines of AK rifles, two grenades and two gloves where the fence had been cut.

Heading: 4 BSF men injured - Indian Express
Content:
Entries are now open for the Ramnath Goenka India Press Photo Awards 2008. Professional press photographers, photojournalists and documentary photographers are invited to send in pictures that show outstanding visual qualities and tell a news story with great force. The Ramnath Goenka Picture of the Year Award will honour the entry that demonstrates an outstanding level of visual creativity and journalistic skill.

The winning photographer will receive a cash prize of Rs 1.5 lakh. Entries are open for pictures taken between January 1, 2006 and December 31, 2007, and are intended for publication. The deadline for submitting entries by post is September 30, 2008.

The Awards, instituted by the Ramnath Goenka Foundation, are being presented by Canon this year. The award-winning photographs will be displayed at an exhibition in Mumbai. For further details, rules and regulations, log on to www.expressindia.com/ippa.

The Express Group initiated the Awards to identify, promote and reward excellence in photojournalism and documentary photography in 2004. Last year, Vipin Pawar of DNA, Mumbai, won the top award for his photograph of the stabbing of a young woman at the Gateway of India.

The awards also invite creative entries in various categories like arts and entertainment and sports apart from spot news, which requires immediate presence and documentation of hard news.

Content: In yet another incident of ceasefire violation, four BSF personnel, including a sub-inspector, were injured as Pakistani troops opened fire across the LoC in Poonch district on Tuesday morning. BSF DIG (G) S Sagwan said the firing took place when a party from the 192 Battalion was patrolling K P Nala Post. Heavy mortar shells along with small-arms fire came from Pakistan's NCPP post at around 4 am forcing the BSF to retaliate.

Heading: She’s reluctant no more, Michelle takes centrestage - Indian Express
Content:
Turning the personal into the political, Democrats opened their presidential nominating convention on Monday with testimonials to Barack Obama as a husband, father, brother and, above all, a leader able to transcend the nation's long divide across racial and gender lines.

It was a parade of the past and future, with Senator Edward M Kennedy of Massachusetts —ailing in the twilight of his 46-year career—vouching for Obama, who dawned on the national scene at the Democrats' convention four years ago.

Playing the role of chief character witness was Obama's wife, Michelle, who cast herself and her husband as symbols of America's potential and its promise.

"I come here as a wife who loves my husband and believes he will be an extraordinary President," Michelle Obama said, though she never mentioned his effort to break the ultimate racial barrier by winning the White House. The getting-to-know-you phase featured several branches of Obama's family tree, including his brother-in-law, his sister and several longtime friends and associates from his adopted home state of Illinois.

Reaching for the transcendence of her husband's 2004 address at the party's last national gathering she declared: "Barack doesn't care where you're from, or what your background is, or what party, if any, you belong to. That's not how he sees the world. He knows that thread that connects us — our belief in America's promise, our commitment to our children's future — is strong enough to hold us together as one nation even when we disagree."

Much of her 20-minute speech was plain-spoken, delivered in a crisp tone. To those who would question her patriotism, as some have, Obama offered a long and passionate paean to America's possibility, ending with the affirmation: "That is why I love this country."

Michelle described meeting her husband and discovering that, despite his "funny name", they shared the same values, in his case instilled by the single mother and grandparents who raised him: "That you work hard for what you want in life; that your word is your bond and you do what you say you're going to do; that you treat people with dignity and respect, even if you don't know them, and even if you don't agree with them."

She also reached out to Clinton's supporters, even before she praised her husband's running mate, Joe Biden, saying the votes cast for New York's senator "put those 18 million cracks in the glass ceiling so that our daughters —and sons — can dream a little bigger and aim a little higher". The crowd roared its approval.

The emotional high point of the evening was a surprise appearance by Kennedy, 76, who is battling brain cancer. He walked across the stage flashing his thumbs up to delegates, who leaped to their feet in an exuberant ovation. When he spoke, his voice was strong. Looking out on a sea of blue-and-white "Kennedy" signs, the snowy-haired senator summoned memories of his brother, the late President John F Kennedy, and the man-on-the-moon challenge he laid down for his countrymen.

Kennedy urged Americans to "rise to our best ideals" in November and offered Obama as the embodiment of that aspiration. "Barack Obama will close the book on the old politics of race and gender, of group against group, of straight against gay," Kennedy said.

The evening ended with a made-for-TV scene of family togetherness, as Obama's image was beamed into the convention hall from Kansas City, where he plans to campaign today.

"Hi, Daddy!" his daughter Sasha, 7, called out to his image on a giant video screen.

"Michelle, you were unbelievable," Obama said. "And you also look very cute."

"That's Sasha," Michelle Obama said.

"Daddy, what city are you in?" Sasha asked.

"I'm in Kansas City, sweetie. And Malia, Sasha, how do you think Mom did?"

"I think she did good," Sasha said.

Obama laughed with the convention audience. "I think so too," he said.

Heading: Hillary’s people cloud Obama show - Indian Express
Content:
When her husband ran for Congress in 2000, Michelle Obama groused so much about handshaking and fundraising that Arthur Sussman, then her boss at the University of Chicago, asked if she truly couldn't find a single thing about campaigning to enjoy.

Michelle Obama thought for a moment. Visiting so many living rooms had given her some new decorating ideas, she allowed.

Eight years later, the once reluctant campaigner is at the centre of a multimedia charm offensive that may be the most closely managed spousal rollout in presidential campaign history. Monday night's prime-time speech was preceded by an intricately made biographical video. Michelle wore a designer dress, but lately she has more often sported a cheap-chic approach to fashion: fewer designer pieces, more $79 Gap sundresses.

But refashioning her own public image is just one of two things she must now do. Worried that Obama's far-flung upbringing and lack of deep roots leave some voters unsure and untrusting, the campaign is substituting her family background for his own.

So on Monday night, the campaign filled stage and screen with Michelle's family — her basketball-coach brother Craig Robinson, homemaker-turned-secretary mom Marian, and memory of her father, Frasier. Her film, South Side Girl, guided by voice-overs from her mom, gave a flattering guided tour of her childhood, romance with Barack Obama, and motherhood.

Ever since Michelle left her job as a hospital administrator, some feminist critics have complained that she sacrificed her own work for her husband's. But from the start, the Obama marriage was a kind of partnership between two ambitious people who found they could rise higher in the world together than alone.

On the evening of the Iowa caucuses, the Obamas gathered with close friends at restaurant in Des Moines, where Michelle stood to give a toast. "Here's to my husband, the man I love and the man I believe would be the best President," she said. Just then, a campaign aide broke in with news: TV was calling the state for Obama. As the room erupted in jubilation, as friends hugged, friends say, Michelle Obama simply looked stunned.

THREAT TO OBAMA?

U S authorities are investigating whether three men arrested in Colorado with guns and drugs planned to kill Barack Obama, but say they posed no real threat. "We're absolutely confident there is no credible threat," U S Attorney Troy Eid said. Local media reported that police in Aurora, east of Denver, found two rifles, ammunition, a bulletproof vest, walkie-talkies and methamphetamine in a rented pickup truck early on Sunday morning. The suspects are Tharin Gartrell, 28, Nathan Johnson, 32, and Shawn Adolf, 33, the reports said.

Heading: Republican fire bears down on rift in Democratic camp - Indian Express
Content:
As Hillary Rodham Clinton prepares to speak on Day 2 of the Democratic Convention, resentment among her supporters — miffed that she lost the nomination and was not picked as Barack Obama's vice-presidential running mate — threatens to rain on the presidential hopeful's parade.

Obama has conceded "there are going to be some of Senator Clinton's supporters who we're going to have to work hard to persuade to come on board," adding "that's not surprising". But he has played down the rift: "I am absolutely convinced that both Hillary Clinton and (her husband, former President) Bill Clinton understand the stakes."

The two camps have come up with a plan to placate Hillary supporters by allowing three speeches on behalf of a symbolic nomination for Hillary before the floor turns to nominating Obama as the Democratic candidate. Bill Clinton will speak on Wednesday.

Hillary, who is expected to urge her delegates to back Obama, has acknowledged the difficulty in bringing everyone in line. "We are after all Democrats, so it may take a while," she said. "We're not the fall-in-line party. We are diverse. But make no mistake, we are unified."

Publicly, the two camps have been placatory. "There is no stronger surrogate for Sen. Obama than Sen. Clinton," Valerie Jarrett, adviser to Obama, said.

Heading: Like a rock concert, with the most famous band in the world - Indian Express
Content:
In a production studio here, a SWAT team of Republican operatives is reveling in its accomplishments.

Two new advertisements devised to stoke the sore feelings of Hillary Clinton's devotees are being widely covered online and on cable TV.

A presser the Republicans produced of former Clinton supporters who said they were now backing John McCain, has drawn a large crowd of reporters.

And a 'Happy Hour for Hillary' party is planned, to be followed by McCain's appearance on Tonight with Jay Leno.

There was a time when a party ceded the stage to the other during its convention, under the assumption that breaking through the news coverage would be next to impossible anyway. Over the past few bitterly partisan election cycles, however, the pattern has disintegrated, helped by a proliferation of new media outlets that created growing opportunities to spread negative messages.

Heading: America raps UN envoy for Zardari ties - Indian Express
Content:
The snow-tipped peaks of the Rockies are visible in the distance toward the West, and a raging tornado touched down within a mile of my hotel soon after my arrival, but the most startling sight of the Democratic convention so far has belonged to George Bush's idea of good government. Half a dozen policemen, in black riot gear, standing on the customized iron boards fixed to the sides of an SUV slowly sliding by the pavements crowded with delegates.

It's quite a sight in the heat. The cops wear Kelvar vests and reinforced knee pads; they have pepper-ball guns strapped to their chest and a revolver at the hip; helmets, billy clubs, a cylinder of mace, are their other accessories; and, thin and shiny blue plastic, meant to tie the hands of those arrested, are coiled a little below the waist. These are the designer police, looking like oversized versions of a nine-year-old boy's fantasy toys.

But there's been hardly any protest: this isn't the season of rage, only of hope. If not for a new future, then at least for a new T-shirt. The Democratic nominee's face has been painted, printed, stenciled by Warhol imitators. Obama might be in Kansas today, but in Denver he is everywhere. In all colours you can imagine. In contrast, the right betrays a muted sense of colour. All the T-shirts I have seen the right-wing protesters wearing here—their backs proclaiming NOBAMA!—are the hue of deep mud.

Downtown Denver is overrun with delegates. But more than delegates there are the members of the press, nearly three times as many. And more than the press, there are the volunteers, twenty six thousand in all. In a T-shirt culture, this means that as a volunteer you get to wear an orange shirt and say "Welcome to Denver." "Thank you," I heard Ted Koppel say, over and over again, as he walked to the Colorado Convention Center this morning.

Perhaps I sound bitter. I have suffered. Each day's press pass is to be given out new, perhaps out of security reasons, and this means long lines. I have spent more time in lines for the press credentials than in doing anything else. Standing for hours in a queue of foreign journalists, in the corridor of the Hampton Inn and Suites, I have become intimate with the faded brown wallpaper, the potted plastic plants, and the smell of disinfectant.

Today, on the first day of the convention, after having done penance in the line at Hampton Inn and Suites, I attended the first-ever meeting of Indian Americans at a political convention. Organized by a group called Indian American Leadership Initiative, the gathering was held in the Denver Athletic Club, its members working out in the next room on treadmills and elliptical machines.

At the Club, I talked to S R Sidarth, the Indian American youth who, during the 2006 Senate election, became the centre of a media storm. Sidarth had been working on the staff of Democratic candidate Jim Webb in his home state of Virginia. One week in August that year, he was given the task of tracking Webb's Republican opponent, Senator George Allen. Sidarth would accompany the Senator on his "listening tour" and videotape his speeches. At one of these meetings, in Breaks Interstate Park, Allen had pointed to Sidarth, and having identified him as "macaca or whatever his name is" proceeded to welcome him "to America and the real world of Virginia."

Allen later denied that he knew that the word "macaca" referred to a species of monkey. He also stressed that he hadn't meant to malign Sidarth as an immigrant. But Allen, who had even harboured Presidential ambitions, never recovered from the storm of controversy. Sidarth appeared on major television channels; his op-ed was published in the Washington Post. Allen lost the election narrowly by about 9,000 votes out of a total of 2.4 million votes cast. In a tight election year, Sidarth was credited for having helped the Democrats regain the Senate by a single seat.

His parents migrated from India more than two decades ago, and Sidarth was born in Arlington, Virginia. He is now 23, working as a Democratic Party staff-member at this convention. Sidarth told me that he believes that the "macaca" incident guided him to his "calling." He will work in politics all his life. His enthusiasm for Senator Obama is based on the fact that as a person from a diverse cultural and racial background, Obama understands the place of immigrants in America. Sidarth says, "His story resonates with Indians."

Sidarth is tall and well-built, with a slightly shy manner, often looking away when making his point. But he was emphatic that there is "unprecedented excitement" about Obama. He said, "This is like a rock concert with the most famous band in the world."

Journalist, author and academic Amitava Kumar is professor of English at Vassar College, New York.

Heading: Presidential candidates file nominations - Indian Express
Content:
Zalmay Khalilzad, the American ambassador to the UN, is facing angry questions from other senior Bush administration officials over what they describe as unauthorised contacts with PPP chief Asif Ali Zardari.

Khalilzad had spoken over telephone with Zardari several times a week in the past month until he was confronted about the unauthorised contacts, a senior US official said.

Other officials said Khalilzad had planned to meet Zardari privately next Tuesday, in a session that was canceled only after Richard A Boucher, the assistant secretary of state for South Asia, learned from Zardari himself that the ambassador was providing "advice and help".

"Can I ask what sort of 'advice and help' you are providing?" Boucher wrote in an e-mail message to Khalilzad. "What sort of channel is this? Governmental, private, personnel?" Copies of the message were sent to others at the highest levels of the State Department. There is concern within the State Department that discussions between Khalilzad and Zardari could leave the impression that the US is taking sides in Pakistan's chaotic internal politics.

The conduct by Khalilzad, who is Afghan by birth, has also raised hackles because of speculation that he might seek to succeed Hamid Karzai as President of Afghanistan. Khalilzad has said he has no plans to seek the Afghan presidency.
